cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a network (in general)?
cards.back: A group of two or more similar things or people interconnected with each other is called network
cards.quote: A group of two or more similar things or people interconnected with each other is called network

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A computer network can include different types of hosts (also called ____) like server, desktop, laptop, cellular phones.
cards.back: A computer network can include different types of hosts (also called nodes) like server, desktop, laptop, cellular phones.
cards.quote: A computer network can include different types of hosts (also called nodes) like server, desktop, laptop, cellular phones.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For communication, data in a network is divided into smaller chunks called ____.
cards.back: For communication, data in a network is divided into smaller chunks called packets.
cards.quote: For communication, data in a network is divided into smaller chunks called packets.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Devices in a network can be connected either through ____ media like cables or ____ media like air.
cards.back: Devices in a network can be connected either through wired media like cables or wireless media like air.
cards.quote: Devices in a network can be connected either through wired media like cables or wireless media like air.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define a node in a communication network.
cards.back: In a communication network, each device that is a part of a network and that can receive, create, store or send data to different network routes is called a node.
cards.quote: In a communication network, each device that is a part of a network and that can receive, create, store or send data to different network routes is called a node.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which devices can act as a node in data communication?
cards.back: In the context of data communication, a node can be a device such as a modem, hub, bridge, switch, router, digital telephone handset, a printer, a computer or a server.
cards.quote: In the context of data communication, a node can be a device such as a modem, hub, bridge, switch, router, digital telephone handset, a printer, a computer or a server.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does interconnectivity of computing devices in a network allow us to do?
cards.back: Interconnectivity of computing devices in a network allows us to exchange information simultaneously with many parties through email, websites, audio/video calls, etc.
cards.quote: Interconnectivity of computing devices in a network allows us to exchange information simultaneously with many parties through email, websites, audio/video calls, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Resource sharing in a network: what does the network allow, with an example?
cards.back: Network allows sharing of resources. For example, a printer can be made available to multiple computers through a network; a networked storage can be accessed by multiple computers.
cards.quote: Network allows sharing of resources. For example, a printer can be made available to multiple computers through a network; a networked storage can be accessed by multiple computers.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Between which two institutions was the first ARPANET message communicated?
cards.back: The first message was communicated between the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and Stanford Research Institute (SRI).
cards.quote: The first message was communicated between the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and Stanford Research Institute (SRI).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define LAN (Local Area Network).
cards.back: LAN is a network that connects a variety of nodes placed at a limited distance ranging from a single room, a floor, an office or a campus having one or more buildings in the same premises.
cards.quote: LAN is a network that connects a variety of nodes placed at a limited distance ranging from a single room, a floor, an office or a campus having one or more buildings in the same premises.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What geographical area can a LAN cover?
cards.back: The geographical area covered by a LAN can range from a single room, a floor, an office having one or more buildings in the same premise, laboratory, a school, college, or university campus.
cards.quote: The geographical area covered by a LAN can range from a single room, a floor, an office having one or more buildings in the same premise, laboratory, a school, college, or university campus.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: LAN is comparatively secure as only ____ in the network can access other computers or shared resources.
cards.back: LAN is comparatively secure as only authentic users in the network can access other computers or shared resources.
cards.quote: LAN is comparatively secure as only authentic users in the network can access other computers or shared resources.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Up to what distance can a LAN be extended?
cards.back: These types of networks can be extended up to 1 km.
cards.quote: These types of networks can be extended up to 1 km.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the data transfer rate in a LAN?
cards.back: Data transfer in LAN is quite high, and usually varies from 10 Mbps (called Ethernet) to 1000 Mbps (called Gigabit Ethernet), where Mbps stands for Megabits per second.
cards.quote: Data transfer in LAN is quite high, and usually varies from 10 Mbps (called Ethernet) to 1000 Mbps (called Gigabit Ethernet), where Mbps stands for Megabits per second.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is Ethernet?
cards.back: Ethernet is a set of rules that decides how computers and other devices connect with each other through cables in a local area network or LAN.
cards.quote: Ethernet is a set of rules that decides how computers and other devices connect with each other through cables in a local area network or LAN.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define MAN (Metropolitan Area Network).
cards.back: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is an extended form of LAN which covers a larger geographical area like a city or a town.
cards.quote: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is an extended form of LAN which covers a larger geographical area like a city or a town.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does the data transfer rate in a MAN compare with a LAN?
cards.back: Data transfer rate in MAN also ranges in Mbps, but it is considerably less as compared to LAN.
cards.quote: Data transfer rate in MAN also ranges in Mbps, but it is considerably less as compared to LAN.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which network type do cable TV network and cable based broadband internet services illustrate?
cards.back: Cable TV network or cable based broadband internet services are examples of MAN.
cards.quote: Cable TV network or cable based broadband internet services are examples of MAN.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Up to what distance can a MAN be extended?
cards.back: This kind of network can be extended up to 30-40 km.
cards.quote: This kind of network can be extended up to 30-40 km.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define WAN (Wide Area Network).
cards.back: Wide Area Network connects computers and other LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.
cards.quote: Wide Area Network connects computers and other LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The Internet is the ____ that connects billions of computers, smartphones and millions of LANs from different continents.
cards.back: The Internet is the largest WAN that connects billions of computers, smartphones and millions of LANs from different continents.
cards.quote: The Internet is the largest WAN that connects billions of computers, smartphones and millions of LANs from different continents.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a modem?
cards.back: Modem stands for “MOdulator DEModulator”. It refers to a device used for conversion between analog signals and digital bits.
cards.quote: Modem stands for “MOdulator DEModulator”. It refers to a device used for conversion between analog signals and digital bits.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What do the modems at the sender’s end and the receiver’s end do?
cards.back: The modem at the sender’s end acts as a modulator that converts the digital data into analog signals. The modem at the receiver’s end acts as a demodulator that converts the analog signals into digital data for the destination node to understand.
cards.quote: The modem at the sender’s end acts as a modulator that converts the digital data into analog signals. The modem at the receiver’s end acts as a demodulator that converts the analog signals into digital data for the destination node to understand.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an Ethernet card (NIC)?
cards.back: Ethernet card, also known as Network Interface Card (NIC card in short) is a network adapter used to set up a wired network.
cards.quote: Ethernet card, also known as Network Interface Card (NIC card in short) is a network adapter used to set up a wired network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What data transfer speeds can Ethernet cards support?
cards.back: Ethernet cards can support data transfer between 10 Mbps and 1 Gbps (1000 Mbps).
cards.quote: Ethernet cards can support data transfer between 10 Mbps and 1 Gbps (1000 Mbps).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Each NIC has a ____, which helps in uniquely identifying the computer on the network.
cards.back: Each NIC has a MAC address, which helps in uniquely identifying the computer on the network.
cards.quote: Each NIC has a MAC address, which helps in uniquely identifying the computer on the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a repeater?
cards.back: A repeater is an analog device that works with signals on the cables to which it is connected. The weakened signal appearing on the cable is regenerated and put back on the cable by a repeater.
cards.quote: A repeater is an analog device that works with signals on the cables to which it is connected. The weakened signal appearing on the cable is regenerated and put back on the cable by a repeater.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an Internet service provider (ISP)?
cards.back: An Internet service provider (ISP) is any organisation that provides services for accessing the Internet.
cards.quote: An Internet service provider (ISP) is any organisation that provides services for accessing the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an Ethernet hub?
cards.back: An Ethernet hub (Figure 10.11) is a network device used to connect different devices through wires. Data arriving on any of the lines are sent out on all the others.
cards.quote: An Ethernet hub (Figure 10.11) is a network device used to connect different devices through wires. Data arriving on any of the lines are sent out on all the others.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The limitation of Hub is that if data from two devices come at the same time, they will ____.
cards.back: The limitation of Hub is that if data from two devices come at the same time, they will collide.
cards.quote: The limitation of Hub is that if data from two devices come at the same time, they will collide.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a switch?
cards.back: A switch is a networking device used to connect multiple computers or communicating devices.
cards.quote: A switch is a networking device used to connect multiple computers or communicating devices.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does a switch decide where to send data?
cards.back: When data arrives, the switch extracts the destination address from the data packet and looks it up in a table to see where to send the packet. Thus, it sends signals to only selected devices instead of sending to all.
cards.quote: When data arrives, the switch extracts the destination address from the data packet and looks it up in a table to see where to send the packet. Thus, it sends signals to only selected devices instead of sending to all.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a switch do with noisy or corrupted signals?
cards.back: A switch does not forward the signals which are noisy or corrupted. It drops such signals and asks the sender to resend it.
cards.quote: A switch does not forward the signals which are noisy or corrupted. It drops such signals and asks the sender to resend it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a router?
cards.back: A router is a network device that can receive the data, analyse it and transmit it to other networks.
cards.quote: A router is a network device that can receive the data, analyse it and transmit it to other networks.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A router connects a ____ to the internet.
cards.back: A router connects a local area network to the internet.
cards.quote: A router connects a local area network to the internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Router vs hub or switch: the difference in capability
cards.back: Compared to a hub or a switch, a router has advanced capabilities as it can analyse the data being carried over a network, decide/alter how it is packaged, and send it to another network of a different type.
cards.quote: Compared to a hub or a switch, a router has advanced capabilities as it can analyse the data being carried over a network, decide/alter how it is packaged, and send it to another network of a different type.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What dual task do home Wi-Fi routers perform?
cards.back: These days, home Wi-Fi routers perform the dual task of a router and a modem/ switch.
cards.quote: These days, home Wi-Fi routers perform the dual task of a router and a modem/ switch.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a gateway?
cards.back: Gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through the gateway in order to use routing paths.
cards.quote: Gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through the gateway in order to use routing paths.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: As the term “Gateway” suggests, it is a ____ that acts as a “gate” between an organisation's network and the outside world of the Internet
cards.back: As the term “Gateway” suggests, it is a key access point that acts as a “gate” between an organisation's network and the outside world of the Internet
cards.quote: As the term “Gateway” suggests, it is a key access point that acts as a “gate” between an organisation's network and the outside world of the Internet

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does a node communicate with a node of a foreign network?
cards.back: If a node from one network wants to communicate with a node of a foreign network, it will pass the data packet to the gateway, which then routes it to the destination using the best possible route.
cards.quote: If a node from one network wants to communicate with a node of a foreign network, it will pass the data packet to the gateway, which then routes it to the destination using the best possible route.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Generally, a ____ is configured to work as a gateway device in computer networks.
cards.back: Generally, a router is configured to work as a gateway device in computer networks.
cards.quote: Generally, a router is configured to work as a gateway device in computer networks.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Because a network gateway is placed at the edge of a network, the ____ is usually integrated with it.
cards.back: Because a network gateway is placed at the edge of a network, the firewall is usually integrated with it.
cards.quote: Because a network gateway is placed at the edge of a network, the firewall is usually integrated with it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define network topology.
cards.back: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its topology.
cards.quote: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its topology.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Common network topologies
cards.back:
Mesh
Ring
Bus
Star
Tree
cards.quote: Common network topologies are Mesh, Ring, Bus, Star and Tree.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is mesh topology?
cards.back: In mesh topology each communicating device is connected with every other device in the network.
cards.quote: In mesh topology each communicating device is connected with every other device in the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Mesh topology: what are its advantages?
cards.back: Such a network can handle large amounts of traffic since multiple nodes can transmit data simultaneously. Also, such networks are more reliable in the sense that even if a node gets down, it does not cause any break in the transmission of data between other nodes. This topology is also more secure as compared to other topologies because each cable between two nodes carries different data.
cards.quote: Such a network can handle large amounts of traffic since multiple nodes can transmit data simultaneously. Also, such networks are more reliable in the sense that even if a node gets down, it does not cause any break in the transmission of data between other nodes. This topology is also more secure as compared to other topologies because each cable between two nodes carries different data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Mesh topology: what is its disadvantage?
cards.back: However, wiring is complex and cabling cost is high in creating such networks and there are many redundant or unutilised connections.
cards.quote: However, wiring is complex and cabling cost is high in creating such networks and there are many redundant or unutilised connections.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Formula: wires needed for a fully-connected mesh of n nodes
cards.back: To build a fully-connected mesh topology of n nodes, it requires n(n-1)/2 wires.
cards.quote: To build a fully-connected mesh topology of n nodes, it requires n(n-1)/2 wires.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is ring topology?
cards.back: In ring topology, each node is connected to two other devices, one each on either side.
cards.quote: In ring topology, each node is connected to two other devices, one each on either side.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The link in a ring topology is ____. Thus, data can be transmitted in one direction only (clockwise or counterclockwise).
cards.back: The link in a ring topology is unidirectional. Thus, data can be transmitted in one direction only (clockwise or counterclockwise).
cards.quote: The link in a ring topology is unidirectional. Thus, data can be transmitted in one direction only (clockwise or counterclockwise).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is bus topology?
cards.back: In bus topology, a single backbone wire called bus is shared among the nodes, which makes it cheaper and easy to maintain.
cards.quote: In bus topology, a single backbone wire called bus is shared among the nodes, which makes it cheaper and easy to maintain.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Data sent from a node are passed on to the bus and hence are transmitted to the length of the bus in ____.
cards.back: Data sent from a node are passed on to the bus and hence are transmitted to the length of the bus in both directions.
cards.quote: Data sent from a node are passed on to the bus and hence are transmitted to the length of the bus in both directions.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is star topology?
cards.back: In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central networking device like a hub or a switch.
cards.quote: In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central networking device like a hub or a switch.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Star topology: its strength and its weakness
cards.back: Star topology is considered very effective, efficient and fast as each device is directly connected with the central device. Although disturbance in one device will not affect the rest of the network, any failure in a central networking device may lead to the failure of complete network.
cards.quote: Star topology is considered very effective, efficient and fast as each device is directly connected with the central device. Although disturbance in one device will not affect the rest of the network, any failure in a central networking device may lead to the failure of complete network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is tree or hybrid topology?
cards.back: In tree or hybrid topology, there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus.
cards.quote: In tree or hybrid topology, there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Where is tree or hybrid topology usually realised?
cards.back: It is a hierarchical topology, in which there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus. Such topologies are usually realised in WANs where multiple LANs are connected.
cards.quote: It is a hierarchical topology, in which there are multiple branches and each branch can have one or more basic topologies like star, ring and bus. Such topologies are usually realised in WANs where multiple LANs are connected.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does data travel in a tree topology?
cards.back: In this type of network, data transmitted from source first reaches the centralised device and from there the data passes through every branch where each branch can have links for more nodes.
cards.quote: In this type of network, data transmitted from source first reaches the centralised device and from there the data passes through every branch where each branch can have links for more nodes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a MAC address?
cards.back: The MAC address, also known as the physical or hardware address, is a unique permanent value associated with a network adapter called a NIC. It is used to physically identify a machine on the network.
cards.quote: The MAC address, also known as the physical or hardware address, is a unique permanent value associated with a network adapter called a NIC. It is used to physically identify a machine on the network.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: MAC stands for ____.
cards.back: MAC stands for Media Access Control.
cards.quote: MAC stands for Media Access Control.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The MAC address is engraved on NIC at the time of ____ and thus it is a permanent address and cannot be changed under any circumstances.
cards.back: The MAC address is engraved on NIC at the time of manufacturing and thus it is a permanent address and cannot be changed under any circumstances.
cards.quote: The MAC address is engraved on NIC at the time of manufacturing and thus it is a permanent address and cannot be changed under any circumstances.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Describe the structure of a MAC address.
cards.back: Each MAC address is a 12-digit hexadecimal numbers (48 bits in length), of which the first six digits (24 bits) contain the manufacturer’s ID called Organisational Unique Identifier (OUI) and the later six digits (24 bits) represents the serial number assigned to the card by the manufacturer.
cards.quote: Each MAC address is a 12-digit hexadecimal numbers (48 bits in length), of which the first six digits (24 bits) contain the manufacturer’s ID called Organisational Unique Identifier (OUI) and the later six digits (24 bits) represents the serial number assigned to the card by the manufacturer.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an IP address?
cards.back: IP address, also known as Internet Protocol address, is a unique address that can be used to uniquely identify each node in a network.
cards.quote: IP address, also known as Internet Protocol address, is a unique address that can be used to uniquely identify each node in a network.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: MAC address vs IP address: the difference on whether the address changes
cards.back: Unlike MAC address, IP address can change if a node is removed from one network and connected to another network.
cards.quote: Unlike MAC address, IP address can change if a node is removed from one network and connected to another network.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an IPv4 address?
cards.back: The initial IP Address called version 4 (IPV4 in short), is a 32 bit numeric address, written as four numbers separated by periods, where each number is the decimal (base-10) representation for an 8-bit binary (base-2) number and each can take any value from 0 - 255.
cards.quote: The initial IP Address called version 4 (IPV4 in short), is a 32 bit numeric address, written as four numbers separated by periods, where each number is the decimal (base-10) representation for an 8-bit binary (base-2) number and each can take any value from 0 - 255.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Why was IPv6 needed in place of 32-bit IPv4?
cards.back: With more and more devices getting connected to the Internet, it was realised that the 32-bit IP address will not be sufficient as it offers just under 4.3 billion unique addresses.
cards.quote: With more and more devices getting connected to the Internet, it was realised that the 32-bit IP address will not be sufficient as it offers just under 4.3 billion unique addresses.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an IPv6 address?
cards.back: Thus, a 128 bits IP address, called IP version 6 (IPV6 in short) was proposed. An IPv6 address is represented by eight groups of hexadecimal (base-16) numbers separated by colons.
cards.quote: Thus, a 128 bits IP address, called IP version 6 (IPV6 in short) was proposed. An IPv6 address is represented by eight groups of hexadecimal (base-16) numbers separated by colons.

source.section: Identifying Nodes in a Networked Communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the Internet?
cards.back: The Internet is the global network of computing devices.
cards.quote: The Internet is the global network of computing devices.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How do ISPs, regional networks and national networks form the Internet backbone?
cards.back: Many such ISPs connect together forming a regional network and regional networks connect together forming a national network, and such country-wise networks form the Internet backbone.
cards.quote: Many such ISPs connect together forming a regional network and regional networks connect together forming a national network, and such country-wise networks form the Internet backbone.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the World Wide Web (WWW)?
cards.back: The World Wide Web (WWW) or web in short, is an ocean of information, stored in the form of trillions of interlinked web pages and web resources.
cards.quote: The World Wide Web (WWW) or web in short, is an ocean of information, stored in the form of trillions of interlinked web pages and web resources.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who invented the World Wide Web, and in which year?
cards.back: Sir Tim Berners-Lee – a British computer scientist invented the revolutionary World Wide Web in 1990.
cards.quote: Sir Tim Berners-Lee – a British computer scientist invented the revolutionary World Wide Web in 1990.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is HTML?
cards.back: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is a language which is used to design standardised Web Pages so that the Web contents can be read and understood from any computer.
cards.quote: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is a language which is used to design standardised Web Pages so that the Web contents can be read and understood from any computer.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are URI and URL?
cards.back: URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) or URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a unique address or path for each resource located on the web.
cards.quote: URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) or URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a unique address or path for each resource located on the web.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is HTTP, and what is HTTPS?
cards.back: HTTP – The HyperText Transfer Protocol is a set of rules which is used to retrieve linked web pages across the web. The more secure and advanced version is HTTPS.
cards.quote: HTTP – The HyperText Transfer Protocol is a set of rules which is used to retrieve linked web pages across the web. The more secure and advanced version is HTTPS.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Internet vs web: the difference
cards.back: The Internet as we know is the huge global network of interconnected computers, which may or may not have any file or webpage to share with the world. The web on the other hand is the interlinking of collection of Webpages on these computers which are accessible over the Internet.
cards.quote: The Internet as we know is the huge global network of interconnected computers, which may or may not have any file or webpage to share with the world. The web on the other hand is the interlinking of collection of Webpages on these computers which are accessible over the Internet.

source.section: Internet, Web and the Internet of Things

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are domain names (hostnames)?
cards.back: Each computer server hosting a website or web resource is given a name against its IP address. These names are called the Domain names or hostnames.
cards.quote: Each computer server hosting a website or web resource is given a name against its IP address. These names are called the Domain names or hostnames.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is domain name resolution?
cards.back: Conversion of the domain name of each web server to its corresponding IP address is called domain name resolution. It is done through a server called DNS server.
cards.quote: Conversion of the domain name of each web server to its corresponding IP address is called domain name resolution. It is done through a server called DNS server.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What happens when we enter a URL in a web browser (DNS role)?
cards.back: Thus, when we enter a URL on a web browser, the HTTP protocol approaches a computer server called DNS server to obtain the IP address corresponding to that domain name.
cards.quote: Thus, when we enter a URL on a web browser, the HTTP protocol approaches a computer server called DNS server to obtain the IP address corresponding to that domain name.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A DNS server maintains a ____ of domain names and their corresponding IP addresses.
cards.back: A DNS server maintains a database of domain names and their corresponding IP addresses.
cards.quote: A DNS server maintains a database of domain names and their corresponding IP addresses.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How are DNS servers arranged, and how many root servers are at the top?
cards.back: The DNS servers are placed in hierarchical order. At the top level, there are 13 servers called root servers.
cards.quote: The DNS servers are placed in hierarchical order. At the top level, there are 13 servers called root servers.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What may a DNS server contain, if not the IP address of a domain?
cards.back: A DNS server may contain the IP address corresponding to a domain or it will contain the IP address of other DNS servers, where this domain entry can be searched.
cards.quote: A DNS server may contain the IP address corresponding to a domain or it will contain the IP address of other DNS servers, where this domain entry can be searched.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define data communication.
cards.back: Thus, data communication refers to the exchange of data between two or more networked or connected devices.
cards.quote: Thus, data communication refers to the exchange of data between two or more networked or connected devices.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Data can be any text, image, audio, video, and ____ files.
cards.back: Data can be any text, image, audio, video, and multimedia files.
cards.quote: Data can be any text, image, audio, video, and multimedia files.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____ is an act of sending or receiving data.
cards.back: Communication is an act of sending or receiving data.
cards.quote: Communication is an act of sending or receiving data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the five most important components of data communication.
cards.back:
sender
receiver
communication medium
the message to be communicated
certain rules called protocols
cards.quote: These are sender, receiver, communication medium, the message to be communicated, and certain rules called protocols to be followed during communication.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define sender in data communication.
cards.back: A sender is a computer or any such device which is capable of sending data over a network.
cards.quote: A sender is a computer or any such device which is capable of sending data over a network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define receiver in data communication.
cards.back: A receiver is a computer or any such device which is capable of receiving data from the network.
cards.quote: A receiver is a computer or any such device which is capable of receiving data from the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In computer communication, the sender and receiver are known as ____ in a network.
cards.back: In computer communication, the sender and receiver are known as nodes in a network.
cards.quote: In computer communication, the sender and receiver are known as nodes in a network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define message in data communication.
cards.back: It is the data or information that needs to be exchanged between the sender and the receiver.
cards.quote: It is the data or information that needs to be exchanged between the sender and the receiver.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the communication media in data communication?
cards.back: It is the path through which the message travels between source and destination. It is also called medium or link which is either wired or wireless.
cards.quote: It is the path through which the message travels between source and destination. It is also called medium or link which is either wired or wireless.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are protocols, as a component of data communication?
cards.back: It is a set of rules that need to be followed by the communicating parties in order to have successful and reliable data communication.
cards.quote: It is a set of rules that need to be followed by the communicating parties in order to have successful and reliable data communication.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In data communication, the transmission medium is also known as ____.
cards.back: In data communication, the transmission medium is also known as channel.
cards.quote: In data communication, the transmission medium is also known as channel.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define the capacity of a channel.
cards.back: The capacity of a channel is the maximum amount of signals or traffic that a channel can carry.
cards.quote: The capacity of a channel is the maximum amount of signals or traffic that a channel can carry.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In what terms is the capacity of a channel measured?
cards.back: It is measured in terms of bandwidth and data transfer rate
cards.quote: It is measured in terms of bandwidth and data transfer rate as described below:

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define bandwidth of a channel.
cards.back: Bandwidth of a channel is the range of frequencies available for transmission of data through that channel.
cards.quote: Bandwidth of a channel is the range of frequencies available for transmission of data through that channel.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How is bandwidth related to the data transfer rate?
cards.back: Higher the bandwidth, higher the data transfer rate.
cards.quote: Higher the bandwidth, higher the data transfer rate.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Normally, bandwidth is the difference of ____ and minimum frequency contained in the composite signals.
cards.back: Normally, bandwidth is the difference of maximum and minimum frequency contained in the composite signals.
cards.quote: Normally, bandwidth is the difference of maximum and minimum frequency contained in the composite signals.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Bandwidth is measured in ____ (Hz).
cards.back: Bandwidth is measured in Hertz (Hz).
cards.quote: Bandwidth is measured in Hertz (Hz).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Formula: KHz and MHz in Hz.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define data transfer rate.
cards.back: Data transfer rate is the number of bits transmitted between source and destination in one second.
cards.quote: Data transfer rate is the number of bits transmitted between source and destination in one second.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is data transfer rate also known as, and in what unit is it measured?
cards.back: It is also known as bit rate. It is measured in terms of bits per second (bps).
cards.quote: It is also known as bit rate. It is measured in terms of bits per second (bps).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What do MBps and Mbps stand for?
cards.back: MBps stands for Megabyte per second whereas Mbps stands for Megabit per second.
cards.quote: MBps stands for Megabyte per second whereas Mbps stands for Megabit per second.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define simplex communication.
cards.back: It is a one way or unidirectional communication between two devices in which one device is sender and other one is receiver. Devices use the entire capacity of the link to transmit the data.
cards.quote: It is a one way or unidirectional communication between two devices in which one device is sender and other one is receiver. Devices use the entire capacity of the link to transmit the data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Data entered through a keyboard or audio sent to a speaker are examples of which mode of communication?
cards.back:
Simplex communication
For example, data entered through a keyboard or audio sent to a speaker are one way communications.
cards.quote: For example, data entered through a keyboard or audio sent to a speaker are one way communications.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: With the advent of IoT, controlling home appliances is another example of ____ communication as shown in the Figure 11.3.
cards.back: With the advent of IoT, controlling home appliances is another example of simplex communication as shown in the Figure 11.3.
cards.quote: With the advent of IoT, controlling home appliances is another example of simplex communication as shown in the Figure 11.3.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define half-duplex communication.
cards.back: It is two way or bidirectional communication between two devices in which both the devices can send and receive data or control signals in both directions, but not at the same time
cards.quote: It is two way or bidirectional communication between two devices in which both the devices can send and receive data or control signals in both directions, but not at the same time

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Basically, it is a simplex channel where the direction of transmission can be ____.
cards.back: Basically, it is a simplex channel where the direction of transmission can be switched.
cards.quote: Basically, it is a simplex channel where the direction of transmission can be switched.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A walkie-talkie with a push-to-talk button uses which mode of communication?
cards.back:
Half-duplex communication
Application of such type of communication can be found in walkie-talkie where one can press the push-to-talk button and talk.
cards.quote: Application of such type of communication can be found in walkie-talkie where one can press the push-to-talk button and talk.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define full-duplex communication.
cards.back: It is two way or bidirectional communication in which both devices can send and receive data simultaneously
cards.quote: It is two way or bidirectional communication in which both devices can send and receive data simultaneously

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Mobile phones and landline telephones use which mode of communication?
cards.back:
Full-duplex communication
This type of communication channel is employed to allow simultaneous communication, for example, in our mobile phones and landline telephones.
cards.quote: This type of communication channel is employed to allow simultaneous communication, for example, in our mobile phones and landline telephones.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The capacity of the transmission link is ____ between the signals going in both directions.
cards.back: The capacity of the transmission link is shared between the signals going in both directions.
cards.quote: The capacity of the transmission link is shared between the signals going in both directions.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the two commonly used switching techniques.
cards.back:
Circuit Switching
Packet Switching
cards.quote: Two commonly used switching techniques are — Circuit Switching and Packet Switching.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define circuit switching.
cards.back: In circuit switching, before a communication starts, a dedicated path is identified between the sender and the receiver. This path is a connected sequence of links between network nodes. All packets follow the same path established during the connection.
cards.quote: In circuit switching, before a communication starts, a dedicated path is identified between the sender and the receiver. This path is a connected sequence of links between network nodes. All packets follow the same path established during the connection.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Placing a telephone call in earlier days, over a physical path all the way to the receiver, is an example of which switching technique?
cards.back:
Circuit switching
This is an example of circuit switching.
cards.quote: In earlier days, when we placed a telephone call, the switching equipment within the telephone system finds out a physical path or channel all the way from our telephone at home to the receiver's telephone. This is an example of circuit switching.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define packet switching.
cards.back: In packet switching, each information or message to be transmitted between sender and receiver is broken down into smaller pieces, called packets. These packets are then transmitted independently through the network. Different packets of the same message may take different routes depending on availability.
cards.quote: In packet switching, each information or message to be transmitted between sender and receiver is broken down into smaller pieces, called packets. These packets are then transmitted independently through the network. Different packets of the same message may take different routes depending on availability.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the two parts of a packet.
cards.back:
a header containing the address of the destination and other information
the main message part
cards.quote: Each packet has two parts — a header containing the address of the destination and other information, and the main message part.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: When all the packets reach the destination, they are ____ and the complete message is received by the receiver.
cards.back: When all the packets reach the destination, they are reassembled and the complete message is received by the receiver.
cards.quote: When all the packets reach the destination, they are reassembled and the complete message is received by the receiver.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Circuit vs packet switching: the difference in how the channel is occupied.
cards.back: Unlike circuit switching, a channel is occupied in packet switching only during the transmission of the packet. On completion of the transmission, the channel is available for transfer of packets from other communicating parties.
cards.quote: Unlike circuit switching, a channel is occupied in packet switching only during the transmission of the packet. On completion of the transmission, the channel is available for transfer of packets from other communicating parties.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a transmission medium?
cards.back: A transmission medium can be anything that can carry signals or data between the source (transmitter) and destination (receiver).
cards.quote: A transmission medium can be anything that can carry signals or data between the source (transmitter) and destination (receiver).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define transmission media in data communication.
cards.back: In data communication, transmission media are the links that carry messages between two or more communicating devices.
cards.quote: In data communication, transmission media are the links that carry messages between two or more communicating devices.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Classification of transmission media.
cards.back:
guided
unguided
cards.quote: Transmission can be classified as guided or unguided.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define guided transmission.
cards.back: In guided transmission, there is a physical link made of wire/cable through which data in terms of signals are propagated between the nodes. These are usually metallic cable, fiber-optic cable, etc. They are also known as wired media.
cards.quote: In guided transmission, there is a physical link made of wire/cable through which data in terms of signals are propagated between the nodes. These are usually metallic cable, fiber-optic cable, etc. They are also known as wired media.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define unguided transmission.
cards.back: In unguided transmission, data travels in air in terms of electromagnetic waves using an antenna. They are also known as wireless media.
cards.quote: In unguided transmission, data travels in air in terms of electromagnetic waves using an antenna. They are also known as wireless media.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the three commonly used wired (guided) transmission media.
cards.back:
twisted pair
coaxial cable
fiber optic cable
cards.quote: Three commonly used guided/wired media for data transmission are, twisted pair, coaxial cable, and fiber optic cable.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Twisted-pair and coaxial cable carry the ____ signals whereas the optical fiber cable carries the ____ signals.
cards.back: Twisted-pair and coaxial cable carry the electric signals whereas the optical fiber cable carries the light signals.
cards.quote: Twisted-pair and coaxial cable carry the electric signals whereas the optical fiber cable carries the light signals.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a twisted-pair cable?
cards.back: A twisted-pair consists of two copper wires twisted like a DNA helical structure.
cards.quote: A twisted-pair consists of two copper wires twisted like a DNA helical structure.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The use of ____ configuration minimises the effect of electrical interference from similar pairs close by.
cards.back: The use of twisted configuration minimises the effect of electrical interference from similar pairs close by.
cards.quote: The use of twisted configuration minimises the effect of electrical interference from similar pairs close by.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Twisted pairs are less expensive and most commonly used in ____ and LANs.
cards.back: Twisted pairs are less expensive and most commonly used in telephone lines and LANs.
cards.quote: Twisted pairs are less expensive and most commonly used in telephone lines and LANs.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Types of twisted-pair cable.
cards.back:
Unshielded twisted-pair (UTP)
Shielded twisted-pair (STP)
cards.quote: These cables are of two types: Unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) and Shielded twisted-pair (STP)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Coaxial cable vs twisted pair: the difference in shielding and bandwidth.
cards.back: It is better shielded and has more bandwidth than a twisted pair.
cards.quote: It is better shielded and has more bandwidth than a twisted pair.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Layers of a coaxial cable, from the core outward.
cards.back:
a copper wire at the core of the cable
insulating material
an outer conductor (usually a copper mesh)
a plastic cover
cards.quote: it has a copper wire at the core of the cable which is surrounded with insulating material. The insulator is further surrounded with an outer conductor (usually a copper mesh). This outer conductor is wrapped in a plastic cover.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The key to success of coaxial cable is its ____ design that allows the cable's copper core to transmit data quickly
cards.back: The key to success of coaxial cable is its shielded design that allows the cable's copper core to transmit data quickly
cards.quote: The key to success of coaxial cable is its shielded design that allows the cable's copper core to transmit data quickly

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are backbone networks?
cards.back: Backbone networks interconnect different segments of the network and provide a path to exchange information between different LANs or subnetworks.
cards.quote: Backbone networks interconnect different segments of the network and provide a path to exchange information between different LANs or subnetworks.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define frequency of a wave.
cards.back: The number of oscillations a wave makes per second is called its frequency, and it is measured in Hz (Hertz).
cards.quote: The number of oscillations a wave makes per second is called its frequency, and it is measured in Hz (Hertz).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an optical fibre cable?
cards.back: The optical fiber cable carries data as light, which travels inside a thin fiber of glass
cards.quote: The optical fiber cable carries data as light, which travels inside a thin fiber of glass

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Optic fiber uses ____ to direct the light through the media.
cards.back: Optic fiber uses refraction to direct the light through the media.
cards.quote: Optic fiber uses refraction to direct the light through the media.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A thin transparent strand of glass at the centre is covered with a layer of less dense glass called ____.
cards.back: A thin transparent strand of glass at the centre is covered with a layer of less dense glass called cladding.
cards.quote: A thin transparent strand of glass at the centre is covered with a layer of less dense glass called cladding.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Advantages of optical fibre cable.
cards.back:
light weight
higher bandwidth which means higher data transfer rate
Signals can travel longer distances
electromagnetic noise cannot affect the cable
cards.quote: These cables are of light weight and have higher bandwidth which means higher data transfer rate. Signals can travel longer distances and electromagnetic noise cannot affect the cable.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Disadvantages of optical fibre cable.
cards.back:
optic fibers are expensive
unidirectional
Two cables are required for full duplex communication
cards.quote: However, optic fibers are expensive and unidirectional. Two cables are required for full duplex communication.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Electromagnetic spectrum of frequency ranging from ____ to ____ is available for wireless communication
cards.back: Electromagnetic spectrum of frequency ranging from 3 KHz to 900 THz is available for wireless communication
cards.quote: Electromagnetic spectrum of frequency ranging from 3 KHz to 900 THz is available for wireless communication

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Wireless technologies allow communication between two or more devices in short to long distance without requiring any ____.
cards.back: Wireless technologies allow communication between two or more devices in short to long distance without requiring any physical media.
cards.quote: Wireless technologies allow communication between two or more devices in short to long distance without requiring any physical media.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The four categories of the electromagnetic spectrum used for wireless communication.
cards.back:
Radio waves
Microwaves
Infrared waves
Visible or Light waves
cards.quote: The electromagnetic spectrum range (3KHz to 900THz) can be divided into 4 categories (Figure 11.12) Radio waves, Microwaves, Infrared waves and Visible or Light waves, according to their frequency ranges.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the frequency range of microwaves?
cards.back: Electromagnetic waves of frequency range 1GHz - 300GHz.
cards.quote: Electromagnetic waves of frequency range 1GHz - 300GHz.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Microwaves: omni-directional or unidirectional?
cards.back: Unidirectional, can move in only one direction.
cards.quote: Unidirectional, can move in only one direction.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Can microwaves penetrate solid objects such as walls, hills or mountains?
cards.back: Cannot penetrate solid objects such as walls, hills or mountains.
cards.quote: Cannot penetrate solid objects such as walls, hills or mountains.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What kind of propagation do microwaves need?
cards.back: Needs line-of-sight propagation i.e. both communicating antenna must be in the direction of each other.
cards.quote: Needs line-of-sight propagation i.e. both communicating antenna must be in the direction of each other.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are microwaves used for?
cards.back: Used in point-to-point communication or unicast communication such as radar and satellite.
cards.quote: Used in point-to-point communication or unicast communication such as radar and satellite.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the frequency range of infrared waves?
cards.back: Electromagnetic waves of frequency range 300GHz - 400THz.
cards.quote: Electromagnetic waves of frequency range 300GHz - 400THz.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Can infrared waves penetrate solid objects such as walls?
cards.back: Cannot penetrate solid objects such as walls.
cards.quote: Cannot penetrate solid objects such as walls.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are infrared waves used for?
cards.back: Used for short-distance point-to-point communication such as mobile-to-mobile, mobile-to-printer, remote-control-to-TV, and Bluetooth-enabled devices to other devices like mouse, keyboards etc.
cards.quote: Used for short-distance point-to-point communication such as mobile-to-mobile, mobile-to-printer, remote-control-to-TV, and Bluetooth-enabled devices to other devices like mouse, keyboards etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is Bluetooth?
cards.back: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology that can be used to connect mobile-phones, mouse, headphones, keyboards, computers, etc. wirelessly over a short distance.
cards.quote: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology that can be used to connect mobile-phones, mouse, headphones, keyboards, computers, etc. wirelessly over a short distance.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a piconet?
cards.back: In Bluetooth technology, the communicating devices within a range of 10 meters build a personal area network called piconet.
cards.quote: In Bluetooth technology, the communicating devices within a range of 10 meters build a personal area network called piconet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The devices in a piconet work in a ____ configuration. A master device can communicate with up to ____ active slave devices at the same time.
cards.back: The devices in a piconet work in a master-slave configuration. A master device can communicate with up to 7 active slave devices at the same time.
cards.quote: The devices in a piconet work in a master-slave configuration. A master device can communicate with up to 7 active slave devices at the same time.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Bluetooth technology allows up to ____ devices to build a network.
cards.back: Bluetooth technology allows up to 255 devices to build a network.
cards.quote: Bluetooth technology allows up to 255 devices to build a network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Wireless LAN?
cards.back: Wireless LAN is a local area network (LAN), and it is a popular way to connect to the Internet.
cards.quote: Wireless LAN is a local area network (LAN), and it is a popular way to connect to the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an access point (AP)?
cards.back: An access point is a device that is used to create a wireless local area network, by connecting to a wired router, switch, or hub.
cards.quote: An access point is a device that is used to create a wireless local area network, by connecting to a wired router, switch, or hub.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the benefits of WLAN.
cards.back:
Wireless connections can be used to extend or replace an existing wired infrastructure
Resulted in increased access for mobile devices
Provides easy access to the Internet in public places
cards.quote: Wireless connections can be used to extend or replace an existing wired infrastructure Resulted in increased access for mobile devices Provides easy access to the Internet in public places

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How are the generations of mobile communication technologies identified?
cards.back:
1G
2G
3G
4G
5G
cards.quote: They are identified as 1G, 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The first generation (1G) mobile network system came around ____. It was used to transmit only ____ calls.
cards.back: The first generation (1G) mobile network system came around 1982. It was used to transmit only voice calls.
cards.quote: The first generation (1G) mobile network system came around 1982. It was used to transmit only voice calls.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The second generation (2G) mobile network system came around ____.
cards.back: The second generation (2G) mobile network system came around 1991.
cards.quote: The second generation (2G) mobile network system came around 1991.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Instead of analog signals, voice calls were transmitted in ____ form thus providing improved call quality.
cards.back: Instead of analog signals, voice calls were transmitted in digital form thus providing improved call quality.
cards.quote: Instead of analog signals, voice calls were transmitted in digital form thus providing improved call quality.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The third generation (3G) mobile network technology was developed during late 90s, but it was introduced commercially around ____.
cards.back: The third generation (3G) mobile network technology was developed during late 90s, but it was introduced commercially around 2001.
cards.quote: The third generation (3G) mobile network technology was developed during late 90s, but it was introduced commercially around 2001.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: 3G provided ____ via the same radio towers that provide voice service to the mobile phone.
cards.back: 3G provided Internet access via the same radio towers that provide voice service to the mobile phone.
cards.quote: 3G provided Internet access via the same radio towers that provide voice service to the mobile phone.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: 4G systems support ____, voice, video, wireless internet and other broadband services.
cards.back: 4G systems support interactive multimedia, voice, video, wireless internet and other broadband services.
cards.quote: 4G systems support interactive multimedia, voice, video, wireless internet and other broadband services.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is machine to machine (M2M) communication?
cards.back: Machine to machine (M2M) is direct communication between devices — wired and wireless.
cards.quote: Machine to machine (M2M) is direct communication between devices — wired and wireless.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: 5G is expected to allow data transfer in ____, which is much faster than 4G.
cards.back: 5G is expected to allow data transfer in Gbps, which is much faster than 4G.
cards.quote: 5G is expected to allow data transfer in Gbps, which is much faster than 4G.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define protocol in communication.
cards.back: In communication, Protocol is a set of standard rules that the communicating parties — the sender, the receiver, and all other intermediate devices need to follow.
cards.quote: In communication, Protocol is a set of standard rules that the communicating parties — the sender, the receiver, and all other intermediate devices need to follow.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the reasons why we need protocols.
cards.back:
flow control
access control
addressing
cards.quote: We need protocols for different reasons such as flow control, access control, addressing, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: When is flow control required?
cards.back: Flow control is required when the sender and receiver have different speeds of sending and receiving the data.
cards.quote: Flow control is required when the sender and receiver have different speeds of sending and receiving the data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Why is access control required?
cards.back: Access control is required to decide which nodes in a communication channel will access the link shared among them at a particular instant of time.
cards.quote: Access control is required to decide which nodes in a communication channel will access the link shared among them at a particular instant of time.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What else do protocols define?
cards.back:
how computers identify one another on a network
the form to which the data should be converted for transit
how to decide whether the data received is for that node or to be forwarded to another node
ensuring that all the data have reached the destination without any loss
how to rearrange the packets and process them at the destination
cards.quote: Protocols also define: how computers identify one another on a network. the form to which the data should be converted for transit. how to decide whether the data received is for that node or to be forwarded to another node. ensuring that all the data have reached the destination without any loss. how to rearrange the packets and process them at the destination.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is HTTP?
cards.back: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. It is the primary protocol used to access the World Wide Web.
cards.quote: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. It is the primary protocol used to access the World Wide Web.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who led the development of HTTP, where, and in which year?
cards.back: Tim Berners-Lee led the development of HTTP at CERN in 1989 in collaboration with Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) and the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).
cards.quote: Tim Berners-Lee led the development of HTTP at CERN in 1989 in collaboration with Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) and the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: HTTP is a ____ (also called client-server) protocol that runs over ____.
cards.back: HTTP is a request-response (also called client-server) protocol that runs over TCP.
cards.quote: HTTP is a request-response (also called client-server) protocol that runs over TCP.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The common use of HTTP is between a ____ (client) and a web server (server).
cards.back: The common use of HTTP is between a web browser (client) and a web server (server).
cards.quote: The common use of HTTP is between a web browser (client) and a web server (server).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is hypertext?
cards.back: Hypertext refers to a document that contains images or text that can be linked to another document or text.
cards.quote: Hypertext refers to a document that contains images or text that can be linked to another document or text.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A web page is written using a markup language like ____ and is stored on a web server for access via its URL.
cards.back: A web page is written using a markup language like HTML and is stored on a web server for access via its URL.
cards.quote: A web page is written using a markup language like HTML and is stored on a web server for access via its URL.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is FTP?
cards.back: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is the protocol used for transferring files from one machine to another. Like HTTP, FTP also works on a client-server model.
cards.quote: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is the protocol used for transferring files from one machine to another. Like HTTP, FTP also works on a client-server model.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the issues between two devices that FTP takes care of.
cards.back:
use of different conventions while naming files
representation of text and data in different formats
having different directory structure
cards.quote: FTP takes care of issues between two communicating devices, such as: use of different conventions while naming files. representation of text and data in different formats. having different directory structure

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is PPP (Point to Point Protocol)?
cards.back: PPP is a communication protocol which establishes a dedicated and direct connection between two communicating devices.
cards.quote: PPP is a communication protocol which establishes a dedicated and direct connection between two communicating devices.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is raised if a label asked for in label based indexing is not in the index?
