cards.back: If the file is not in the current working directory, then we need to specify the complete path of the file along with its name.
cards.quote: If the file is not in the current working directory, then we need to specify the complete path of the file along with its name.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is access_mode in open()?
cards.back: The access_mode is an optional argument that represents the mode in which the file has to be accessed by the program. It is also referred to as processing mode.
cards.quote: The access_mode is an optional argument that represents the mode in which the file has to be accessed by the program. It is also referred to as processing mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What do the mode letters <r>, <w>, <+> and <a> mean in file access?
cards.back:
<r> for reading
<w> for writing
<+> for both reading and writing
<a> for appending at the end of an existing file
cards.quote: Here mode means the operation for which the file has to be opened like <r> for reading, <w> for writing, <+> for both reading and writing, <a> for appending at the end of an existing file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the default file access mode in open()?
cards.back: The default is the read mode.
cards.quote: The default is the read mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: By default, files are opened in ____ that means strings can be read or written.
cards.back: By default, files are opened in text mode that means strings can be read or written.
cards.quote: By default, files are opened in text mode that means strings can be read or written.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Files containing non-textual data are opened in ____ that means read/write are performed in terms of bytes.
cards.back: Files containing non-textual data are opened in binary mode that means read/write are performed in terms of bytes.
cards.quote: Files containing non-textual data are opened in binary mode that means read/write are performed in terms of bytes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: File mode <rb>: what does it do?
cards.back: Opens the file in binary and read-only mode.
cards.quote: Opens the file in binary and read-only mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: File mode <r+> or <+r>: what does it do?
cards.back: Opens the file in both read and write mode.
cards.quote: Opens the file in both read and write mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: File mode <wb+> or <+wb>: what does it do?
cards.back: Opens the file in read,write and binary mode.
cards.quote: Opens the file in read,write and binary mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: File mode <a+> or <+a>: what does it do?
cards.back: Opens the file in append and read mode.
cards.quote: Opens the file in append and read mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A file is opened in append and read modes: where is the file object?
cards.back: The file object will be at the end of the file.
cards.quote: In the above statement, the file myfile.txt is opened in append and read modes. The file object will be at the end of the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which method does Python provide to close a file?
cards.back: Once we are done with the read/write operations on a file, it is a good practice to close the file. Python provides a close() method to do so.
cards.quote: Once we are done with the read/write operations on a file, it is a good practice to close the file. Python provides a close() method to do so.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of close() in Python.
cards.back: file_object.close()
cards.quote: The syntax of close() is: file_object.close()

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: While closing a file, the system frees the ____ allocated to it.
cards.back: While closing a file, the system frees the memory allocated to it.
cards.quote: While closing a file, the system frees the memory allocated to it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Python makes sure that any unwritten or unsaved data is ____ (written) to the file before it is closed.
cards.back: Python makes sure that any unwritten or unsaved data is flushed off (written) to the file before it is closed.
cards.quote: Python makes sure that any unwritten or unsaved data is flushed off (written) to the file before it is closed.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The advantage of using with clause is that any file that is opened using this clause is ____, once the control comes outside the with clause.
cards.back: The advantage of using with clause is that any file that is opened using this clause is closed automatically, once the control comes outside the with clause.
cards.quote: The advantage of using with clause is that any file that is opened using this clause is closed automatically, once the control comes outside the with clause.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For writing to a file, we first need to open it in ____.
cards.back: For writing to a file, we first need to open it in write or append mode.
cards.quote: For writing to a file, we first need to open it in write or append mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In append mode, where is new data added and where is the file object?
cards.back: in append mode, new data will be added at the end of the previous data as the file object is at the end of the file.
cards.quote: in append mode, new data will be added at the end of the previous data as the file object is at the end of the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the methods used to write data in a text file.
cards.back:
write() - for writing a single string
writelines() - for writing a sequence of strings
cards.quote: write() - for writing a single string writelines() - for writing a sequence of strings

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the write() method do and what does it return?
cards.back: write() method takes a string as an argument and writes it to the text file. It returns the number of characters being written on single execution of the write() method.
cards.quote: write() method takes a string as an argument and writes it to the text file. It returns the number of characters being written on single execution of the write() method.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How many characters is '\n' treated as?
cards.back: Note: ‘\n’ is treated as a single character
cards.quote: Note: ‘\n’ is treated as a single character

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: If numeric data are to be written to a text file, the data need to be converted into ____ before writing to the file.
cards.back: If numeric data are to be written to a text file, the data need to be converted into string before writing to the file.
cards.quote: If numeric data are to be written to a text file, the data need to be converted into string before writing to the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Where does write() actually write data, and when is it moved to the file?
cards.back: The write() actually writes data onto a buffer. When the close() method is executed, the contents from this buffer are moved to the file located on the permanent storage.
cards.quote: The write() actually writes data onto a buffer. When the close() method is executed, the contents from this buffer are moved to the file located on the permanent storage.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the flush() method do?
cards.back: We can also use the flush() method to clear the buffer and write contents in buffer to the file.
cards.quote: We can also use the flush() method to clear the buffer and write contents in buffer to the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the writelines() method do?
cards.back: writelines() method is used to write multiple strings to a file. We need to pass an iterable object like lists, tuple etc. containing strings to writelines() method.
cards.quote: writelines() method is used to write multiple strings to a file. We need to pass an iterable object like lists, tuple etc. containing strings to writelines() method.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Does writelines() return the number of characters written in the file?
cards.back: the writelines() method does not return the number of characters written in the file.
cards.quote: the writelines() method does not return the number of characters written in the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In which modes must a file be opened before reading it?
cards.quote: Before reading a file, we must make sure that the file is opened in "r", "r+", "w+" or "a+" mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the read() method do?
cards.back: This method is used to read a specified number of bytes of data from a data file.
cards.quote: This method is used to read a specified number of bytes of data from a data file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of the read() method.
cards.back: file_object.read(n)
cards.quote: The syntax of read() method is: file_object.read(n)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: If no argument or a negative number is specified in read(), the ____ is read.
cards.back: If no argument or a negative number is specified in read(), the entire file content is read.
cards.quote: If no argument or a negative number is specified in read(), the entire file content is read.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the readline([n]) method do?
cards.back: This method reads one complete line from a file where each line terminates with a newline (\n) character.
cards.quote: This method reads one complete line from a file where each line terminates with a newline (\n) character.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does readline(n) use n?
cards.back: It can also be used to read a specified number (n) of bytes of data from a file but maximum up to the newline character (\n).
cards.quote: It can also be used to read a specified number (n) of bytes of data from a file but maximum up to the newline character (\n).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does readline(), used in a loop, return when EOF is reached?
cards.back: It returns an empty string when EOF is reached.
cards.quote: To read the entire file line by line using the readline(), we can use a loop. This process is known as looping/ iterating over a file object. It returns an empty string when EOF is reached.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the readlines() method do?
cards.back: The method reads all the lines and returns the lines along with newline as a list of strings.
cards.quote: The method reads all the lines and returns the lines along with newline as a list of strings.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which function displays each word of a line separately as an element of a list?
cards.back: In case we want to display each word of a line separately as an element of a list, then we can use split() function.
cards.quote: In case we want to display each word of a line separately as an element of a list, then we can use split() function.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does splitlines() return compared with split()?
cards.back: However, if splitlines() is used instead of split(), then each line is returned as element of a list
cards.quote: However, if splitlines() is used instead of split(), then each line is returned as element of a list

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which functions let Python access data in a random fashion?
cards.back: But if we want to access data in a random fashion, then Python gives us seek() and tell() functions to do so.
cards.quote: But if we want to access data in a random fashion, then Python gives us seek() and tell() functions to do so.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the tell() method return?
cards.back: This function returns an integer that specifies the current position of the file object in the file.
cards.quote: This function returns an integer that specifies the current position of the file object in the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What kind of position does tell() give?
cards.back: The position so specified is the byte position from the beginning of the file till the current position of the file object.
cards.quote: The position so specified is the byte position from the beginning of the file till the current position of the file object.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of the tell() method.
cards.back: file_object.tell()
cards.quote: The syntax of using tell() is: file_object.tell()

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the seek() method do?
cards.back: This method is used to position the file object at a particular position in a file.
cards.quote: This method is used to position the file object at a particular position in a file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of the seek() method.
cards.back: file_object.seek(offset [, reference_point])
cards.quote: The syntax of seek() is: file_object.seek(offset [, reference_point])

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In seek(), what is offset?
cards.back: offset is the number of bytes by which the file object is to be moved.
cards.quote: offset is the number of bytes by which the file object is to be moved.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In seek(), what does reference_point indicate?
cards.back: reference_point indicates the starting position of the file object.
cards.quote: reference_point indicates the starting position of the file object.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Values of reference_point in seek().
cards.back:
0 - beginning of the file
1 - current position of the file
2 - end of file
cards.quote: 0 - beginning of the file 1 - current position of the file 2 - end of file

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: By default, the value of reference_point is ____, i.e. the offset is counted from the beginning of the file.
cards.back: By default, the value of reference_point is 0, i.e. the offset is counted from the beginning of the file.
cards.quote: By default, the value of reference_point is 0, i.e. the offset is counted from the beginning of the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does fileObject.seek(5,0) do?
cards.back: For example, the statement fileObject.seek(5,0) will position the file object at 5th byte position from the beginning of the file.
cards.quote: For example, the statement fileObject.seek(5,0) will position the file object at 5th byte position from the beginning of the file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: To create a text file, we use the ____ method and provide the filename and the mode.
cards.back: To create a text file, we use the open() method and provide the filename and the mode.
cards.quote: To create a text file, we use the open() method and provide the filename and the mode.

source.section: Creating and Traversing a Text File

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What happens to an existing file's contents when it is opened in write mode (w)?
cards.back: If it is in write mode (w), then all the existing contents of file will be lost, and an empty file will be created with the same name.
cards.quote: If it is in write mode (w), then all the existing contents of file will be lost, and an empty file will be created with the same name.

source.section: Creating and Traversing a Text File

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In write or append mode, what happens if the file does not exist?
cards.back: In both cases, if the file does not exist, then a new empty file will be created.
cards.quote: In both cases, if the file does not exist, then a new empty file will be created.

source.section: Creating and Traversing a Text File

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the Pickle module used for?
cards.back: To save any object structure along with data, Python provides a module called Pickle. The module Pickle is used for serializing and de-serializing any Python object structure.
cards.quote: To save any object structure along with data, Python provides a module called Pickle. The module Pickle is used for serializing and de-serializing any Python object structure.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is serialization?
cards.back: Serialization is the process of transforming data or an object in memory (RAM) to a stream of bytes called byte streams.
cards.quote: Serialization is the process of transforming data or an object in memory (RAM) to a stream of bytes called byte streams.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Serialization process is also called ____.
cards.back: Serialization process is also called pickling.
cards.quote: Serialization process is also called pickling.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is de-serialization (unpickling)?
cards.back: De-serialization or unpickling is the inverse of pickling process where a byte stream is converted back to Python object.
cards.quote: De-serialization or unpickling is the inverse of pickling process where a byte stream is converted back to Python object.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which kind of files does the pickle module deal with, and what are the words used for writing and reading?
cards.back: The pickle module deals with binary files. Here, data are not written but dumped and similarly, data are not read but loaded.
cards.quote: The pickle module deals with binary files. Here, data are not written but dumped and similarly, data are not read but loaded.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The Pickle Module must be ____ to load and dump data.
cards.back: The Pickle Module must be imported to load and dump data.
cards.quote: The Pickle Module must be imported to load and dump data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The pickle module provides two methods - ____ and ____ to work with binary files for pickling and unpickling, respectively.
cards.back: The pickle module provides two methods - dump() and load() to work with binary files for pickling and unpickling, respectively.
cards.quote: The pickle module provides two methods - dump() and load() to work with binary files for pickling and unpickling, respectively.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the dump() method do, and in which mode must the file be opened?
cards.back: This method is used to convert (pickling) Python objects for writing data in a binary file. The file in which data are to be dumped, needs to be opened in binary write mode (wb).
cards.quote: This method is used to convert (pickling) Python objects for writing data in a binary file. The file in which data are to be dumped, needs to be opened in binary write mode (wb).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of dump() in the pickle module.
cards.back: dump(data_object, file_object)
cards.quote: Syntax of dump() is as follows: dump(data_object, file_object)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the load() method do, and in which mode must the file be opened?
cards.back: This method is used to load (unpickling) data from a binary file. The file to be loaded is opened in binary read (rb) mode.
cards.quote: This method is used to load (unpickling) data from a binary file. The file to be loaded is opened in binary read (rb) mode.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Syntax of load() in the pickle module.
cards.back: Store_object = load(file_object)
cards.quote: Syntax of load() is as follows: Store_object = load(file_object)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Each ____ of a text file represents a character.
cards.back: Each byte of a text file represents a character.
cards.quote: Each byte of a text file represents a character.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a binary file (chapter summary)?
cards.back: Binary file consists of data stored as a stream of bytes.
cards.quote: Binary file consists of data stored as a stream of bytes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does open() do (chapter summary)?
cards.back: open() method is used to open a file in Python and it returns a file object called file handle.
cards.quote: open() method is used to open a file in Python and it returns a file object called file handle.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does close() do (chapter summary)?
cards.back: close() method is used to close the file. While closing a file, the system frees up all the resources like processor and memory allocated to it.
cards.quote: close() method is used to close the file. While closing a file, the system frees up all the resources like processor and memory allocated to it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is pickling (chapter summary)?
cards.back: Pickling is the process by which a Python object is converted to a byte stream.
cards.quote: Pickling is the process by which a Python object is converted to a byte stream.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does dump() do (chapter summary)?
cards.back: dump() method is used to write the objects in a binary file.
cards.quote: dump() method is used to write the objects in a binary file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does load() do (chapter summary)?
cards.back: load() method is used to read data from a binary file.
cards.quote: load() method is used to read data from a binary file.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In data communication, which devices can a node be?
cards.back:
modem
hub
bridge
switch
router
digital telephone handset
a printer
a computer
a server
cards.quote: In the context of data communication, a node can be a device such as a modem, hub, bridge, switch, router, digital telephone handset, a printer, a computer or a server.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Types of computer networks by geographical area covered and data transfer rate
cards.back:
LAN (Local Area Network)
MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)
WAN (Wide Area Network)
cards.quote: Based on the geographical area covered and data transfer rate, computer networks are broadly categorised as: LAN (Local Area Network) MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) WAN (Wide Area Network)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Local Area Network (LAN)?
cards.back: It is a network that connects computers, mobile phones, tablet, mouse, printer, etc., placed at a limited distance.
cards.quote: It is a network that connects computers, mobile phones, tablet, mouse, printer, etc., placed at a limited distance.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the means by which LAN connectivity is done.
cards.back:
wires
Ethernet cables
fibre optics
Wi-Fi
cards.quote: The connectivity is done by means of wires, Ethernet cables, fibre optics, or Wi-Fi.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Give examples of a MAN.
cards.back: Cable TV network or cable based broadband internet services are examples of MAN.
cards.quote: Cable TV network or cable based broadband internet services are examples of MAN.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Wide Area Network (WAN)?
cards.back: Wide Area Network (WAN) connects computers and others LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.
cards.quote: Wide Area Network (WAN) connects computers and others LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: MAN vs WAN: what each one is
cards.back: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is an extended form of LAN which covers a larger geographical area like a city or a town. Wide Area Network (WAN) connects computers and other LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.
cards.quote: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is an extended form of LAN which covers a larger geographical area like a city or a town. Wide Area Network (WAN) connects computers and other LANs and MANs, which are spread across different geographical locations of a country or in different countries or continents.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The modem at the sender’s end acts as a ____ that converts the digital data into analog signals.
cards.back: The modem at the sender’s end acts as a modulator that converts the digital data into analog signals.
cards.quote: The modem at the sender’s end acts as a modulator that converts the digital data into analog signals.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The modem at the receiver’s end acts as a ____ that converts the analog signals into digital data for the destination node to understand.
cards.back: The modem at the receiver’s end acts as a demodulator that converts the analog signals into digital data for the destination node to understand.
cards.quote: The modem at the receiver’s end acts as a demodulator that converts the analog signals into digital data for the destination node to understand.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an Ethernet card?
cards.back: Ethernet card, also known as Network Interface Card (NIC card in short) is a network adaptor used to set up a wired network.
cards.quote: Ethernet card, also known as Network Interface Card (NIC card in short) is a network adaptor used to set up a wired network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a hub?
cards.back: A hub is a network device used to connect multiple devices to form a network or to connect segment(s) of LAN.
cards.quote: A hub is a network device used to connect multiple devices to form a network or to connect segment(s) of LAN.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the limitation of a hub when two devices send data at the same time?
cards.back: if data from two devices come at the same time, they will collide.
cards.quote: if data from two devices come at the same time, they will collide.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: When data arrives, the switch extracts the ____ from the data packet and looks it up in a table to see where to send the packet.
cards.back: When data arrives, the switch extracts the destination address from the data packet and looks it up in a table to see where to send the packet.
cards.quote: When data arrives, the switch extracts the destination address from the data packet and looks it up in a table to see where to send the packet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Gateway serves as the ____ of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through the gateway
cards.back: Gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through the gateway
cards.quote: Gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through the gateway

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Router vs Gateway: what each one is
cards.back: A router is a network device that can receive the data, analyse it and transmit to other networks. A gateway is a device that connects the organisation’s network with the outside world of the Internet.
cards.quote: A router is a network device that can receive the data, analyse it and transmit to other networks. A gateway is a device that connects the organisation’s network with the outside world of the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its ____.
cards.back: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its topology.
cards.quote: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its topology.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the disadvantages of mesh topology.
cards.back:
wiring is complex
cabling cost is high
there are many redundant or unutilised connections
cards.quote: wiring is complex and cabling cost is high in creating such networks, and there are many redundant or unutilised connections.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In this topology, a single backbone wire called bus is shared among the nodes, which makes it ____ and easy to maintain.
cards.back: In this topology, a single backbone wire called bus is shared among the nodes, which makes it cheaper and easy to maintain.
cards.quote: In this topology, a single backbone wire called bus is shared among the nodes, which makes it cheaper and easy to maintain.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In tree topology, multiple star and bus topologies are connected to a central cable, also called the ____ of the network.
cards.back: In tree topology, multiple star and bus topologies are connected to a central cable, also called the backbone of the network.
cards.quote: In tree topology, multiple star and bus topologies are connected to a central cable, also called the backbone of the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Bus vs Star topology: how each connects devices
cards.back: In bus topology, each communicating device connects to a common central transmission medium, known as bus. In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central node, which is a networking device like a hub or a switch, through separate cables.
cards.quote: In bus topology, each communicating device connects to a common central transmission medium, known as bus. In star topology, each communicating device is connected to a central node, which is a networking device like a hub or a switch, through separate cables.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name some services provided through the Internet.
cards.back:
information sharing
communication
data transfer
social networking
e-commerce
cards.quote: Some of the services provided through the Internet are information sharing, communication, data transfer, social networking, e-commerce, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the broad areas or services provided through the Internet.
cards.back:
The World Wide Web (WWW)
Electronic mail (Email)
Chat
Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP)
cards.quote: Following are some of the broad areas or services provided through Internet: The World Wide Web (WWW) Electronic mail (Email) Chat Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a URI?
cards.back: Uniform Resource Identifier or URI is a unique identifier to identify a resource located on the web.
cards.quote: Uniform Resource Identifier or URI is a unique identifier to identify a resource located on the web.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a URL?
cards.back: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a standard naming convention used for accessing resources over the Internet.
cards.quote: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a standard naming convention used for accessing resources over the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In http://www.ncert.nic.in/textbook/textbook.htm: protocol, subdomain, domain name?
cards.back:
http is the protocol name
www is a subdomain
ncert.nic.in is the domain name
cards.quote: In the above URL, http is the protocol name, it can be https, http, FTP, Telnet, etc. www is a subdomain. ncert.nic.in is the domain name.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Internet vs web: what each one is
cards.back: The Internet as we know is the huge global network of interconnected computers, which may or may not have any file or webpage to share with the world. The web on the other hand is the interlinking of a collection of WebPages on these computers which are accessible over the Internet.
cards.quote: The Internet as we know is the huge global network of interconnected computers, which may or may not have any file or webpage to share with the world. The web on the other hand is the interlinking of a collection of WebPages on these computers which are accessible over the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____ like google.co.in, bing.com, duckduckgo.com, in.yahoo.com, etc., can be used to search and retrieve information
cards.back: Search Engine(s) like google.co.in, bing.com, duckduckgo.com, in.yahoo.com, etc., can be used to search and retrieve information
cards.quote: Search Engine(s) like google.co.in, bing.com, duckduckgo.com, in.yahoo.com, etc., can be used to search and retrieve information

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is email?
cards.back: Email is the short form of electronic mail. It is one of the ways of sending and receiving message(s) using the Internet.
cards.quote: Email is the short form of electronic mail. It is one of the ways of sending and receiving message(s) using the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Common facilities for an email user (1 to 5)
cards.back:
Creating an email, attaching files with an email, saving an email as draft for mailing later
Sending and receiving mail
Sending the copy of mail, as carbon copy (cc) or blind carbon copy (bcc)
Forwarding a received email to other user(s)
Filtering spam emails
cards.quote: Following are some of the common facilities available for an email user: 1. Creating an email, attaching files with an email, saving an email as draft for mailing later. Creating email is also termed as composing. 2. Sending and receiving mail. Same email can be sent to multiple email addresses, simultaneously. 3. Sending the copy of mail, as carbon copy (cc) or blind carbon copy (bcc). 4. Forwarding a received email to other user(s) 5. Filtering spam emails

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Common facilities for an email user (6 to 10)
cards.back:
Organising email in folders and sub folders
Creating and managing email ids of the people you know
Setting signature/footer to be inserted automatically at the end of each email
Printing emails using a printer or saving as files
Searching emails using email address or email subject text
cards.quote: 6. Organising email in folders and sub folders 7. Creating and managing email ids of the people you know. 8. Setting signature/footer to be inserted automatically at the end of each email 9. Printing emails using a printer or saving as files. 10. Searching emails using email address or email subject text

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is chatting or Instant Messaging (IM)?
cards.back: Chatting or Instant Messaging (IM) over the Internet means communicating to people at different geographic locations in real time through text message(s).
cards.quote: Chatting or Instant Messaging (IM) over the Internet means communicating to people at different geographic locations in real time through text message(s).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is VoIP?
cards.back: Voice over Internet Protocol or VoIP, allows us to have voice call (telephone service) over the Internet, i.e., the voice transmission over a computer network rather than through the regular telephone network.
cards.quote: Voice over Internet Protocol or VoIP, allows us to have voice call (telephone service) over the Internet, i.e., the voice transmission over a computer network rather than through the regular telephone network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: By what other names is VoIP known?
cards.back: It is also known as Internet Telephony or Broadband Telephony.
cards.quote: It is also known as Internet Telephony or Broadband Telephony.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: VoIP works on the simple principle of converting the ____ voice signals into ____ and then transmitting them over the broadband line.
cards.back: VoIP works on the simple principle of converting the analogue voice signals into digital and then transmitting them over the broadband line.
cards.quote: VoIP works on the simple principle of converting the analogue voice signals into digital and then transmitting them over the broadband line.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the only disadvantage of VoIP?
cards.back: The only disadvantage of VoIP is that its call quality is dependent on Internet connection speed.
cards.quote: The only disadvantage of VoIP is that its call quality is dependent on Internet connection speed.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a website?
cards.back: A website (usually referred to as a site in short) is a collection of web pages related through hyperlinks, and saved on a web server.
cards.quote: A website (usually referred to as a site in short) is a collection of web pages related through hyperlinks, and saved on a web server.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: To access a website, one has to type the address of the website (URL) in the ____ of a browser, and press enter.
cards.back: To access a website, one has to type the address of the website (URL) in the address bar of a browser, and press enter.
cards.quote: To access a website, one has to type the address of the website (URL) in the address bar of a browser, and press enter.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a web page?
cards.back: A web page (also referred to as a page) is a document on the WWW that is viewed in a web browser.
cards.quote: A web page (also referred to as a page) is a document on the WWW that is viewed in a web browser.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Basic structure of a web page is created using ____ (HyperText Markup Language) and ____ (Cascaded Style Sheet).
cards.back: Basic structure of a web page is created using HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascaded Style Sheet).
cards.quote: Basic structure of a web page is created using HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascaded Style Sheet).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the forms of information a web page may contain.
cards.back:
text in the form of paragraphs, lists, tables, etc.
images
audio
video
software application
other interactive contents
cards.quote: A web page is usually a part of a website and may contain information in different forms, such as: text in the form of paragraphs, lists, tables, etc. images audio video software application other interactive contents

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Further, program codes called ____ are used to define the manner in which the page will behave on different actions.
cards.back: Further, program codes called scripts are used to define the manner in which the page will behave on different actions.
cards.quote: Further, program codes called scripts are used to define the manner in which the page will behave on different actions.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____ is the most popular and commonly used scripting language.
cards.back: JavaScript is the most popular and commonly used scripting language.
cards.quote: JavaScript is the most popular and commonly used scripting language.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The first page of the website is called a ____.
cards.back: The first page of the website is called a home page.
cards.quote: The first page of the website is called a home page.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a static web page?
cards.back: A static webpage is one whose content always remains static, i.e., does not change for person to person.
cards.quote: A static webpage is one whose content always remains static, i.e., does not change for person to person.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a web server do on receiving a request for a static web page?
cards.back: it just locates the page on its storage media and sends it to the browser of the client. No additional processing is performed on the page.
cards.quote: it just locates the page on its storage media and sends it to the browser of the client. No additional processing is performed on the page.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a dynamic web page?
cards.back: On the other hand, a dynamic web page is one in which the content of the web page can be different for different users.
cards.quote: On the other hand, a dynamic web page is one in which the content of the web page can be different for different users.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What may a server do before sending a dynamic web page?
cards.back: Before sending the requested web page, the server may perform some additional processes like getting information from the database, updating date and time, updating weather information, etc.
cards.quote: Before sending the requested web page, the server may perform some additional processes like getting information from the database, updating date and time, updating weather information, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Give common examples of dynamic web pages.
cards.back: Few common examples of dynamic web pages are those web pages displaying the date, time, and weather report or having e-commerce applications.
cards.quote: Few common examples of dynamic web pages are those web pages displaying the date, time, and weather report or having e-commerce applications.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Static vs Dynamic web pages: what each one is
cards.back: A static web page is one whose content does not change for requests made by different people. A dynamic web page is one in which the content of the web page displayed is different for different users.
cards.quote: A static web page is one whose content does not change for requests made by different people. A dynamic web page is one in which the content of the web page displayed is different for different users.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Website vs Web page: what each one is
cards.back: A website is a collection of related web pages. A web page is a document that is viewed in a web browser such as Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, Internet Explorer, etc. It can be static or dynamic.
cards.quote: A website is a collection of related web pages. A web page is a document that is viewed in a web browser such as Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, Internet Explorer, etc. It can be static or dynamic.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a web server?
cards.back: A web server is used to store and deliver the contents of a website to clients such as a browser that request it. A web server can be software or hardware.
cards.quote: A web server is used to store and deliver the contents of a website to clients such as a browser that request it. A web server can be software or hardware.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a web server send if it cannot locate the requested page?
cards.back: If the server is not able to locate the page, it sends a page containing the error message (Error 404 – page not found) to the client’s browser.
cards.quote: If the server is not able to locate the page, it sends a page containing the error message (Error 404 – page not found) to the client’s browser.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is web hosting?
cards.back: Web hosting is a service that allows us to put a website or a web page onto the Internet, and make it a part of the World Wide Web.
cards.quote: Web hosting is a service that allows us to put a website or a web page onto the Internet, and make it a part of the World Wide Web.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the domain name system (DNS)?
cards.back: The domain name system (DNS) is a service that does the mapping between domain name and IP address.
cards.quote: The domain name system (DNS) is a service that does the mapping between domain name and IP address.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a browser?
cards.back: A browser is a software application that helps us to view the web page(s).
cards.quote: A browser is a software application that helps us to view the web page(s).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which was the first web browser, and who developed it?
cards.back: Mosaic was the first web browser developed by the National Centre for Supercomputing Application (NCSA).
cards.quote: Mosaic was the first web browser developed by the National Centre for Supercomputing Application (NCSA).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the aspects browser settings may cover.
cards.back:
privacy
search engine preferences
download options
auto signature
autofill and autocomplete feature
theme
cards.quote: These settings may be with respect to privacy, search engine preferences, download options, auto signature, autofill and autocomplete feature, theme and much more.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are add-ons and plug-ins?
cards.back: Add-ons and plug-ins are the tools that help to extend and modify the functionality of the browser.
cards.quote: Add-ons and plug-ins are the tools that help to extend and modify the functionality of the browser.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a plug-in?
cards.back: A plug-in is a complete program or may be a third-party software.
cards.quote: A plug-in is a complete program or may be a third-party software.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an add-on?
cards.back: an add-on is not a complete program and so is used to add only a particular functionality to the browser.
cards.quote: an add-on is not a complete program and so is used to add only a particular functionality to the browser.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: An add-on is also referred to as ____ in some browsers.
cards.back: An add-on is also referred to as extension in some browsers.
cards.quote: An add-on is also referred to as extension in some browsers.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a cookie?
cards.back: A cookie is a text file, containing a string of information, which is transferred by the website to the browser when we browse it.
cards.quote: A cookie is a text file, containing a string of information, which is transferred by the website to the browser when we browse it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Cookies are usually ____ and they can’t access information from the hard disk of a user or transmit virus or malware.
cards.back: Cookies are usually harmless and they can’t access information from the hard disk of a user or transmit virus or malware.
cards.quote: Cookies are usually harmless and they can’t access information from the hard disk of a user or transmit virus or malware.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: One can disable cookies by changing the ____ settings of our browser.
cards.back: One can disable cookies by changing the Privacy and Security settings of our browser.
cards.quote: One can disable cookies by changing the Privacy and Security settings of our browser.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is data visualisation?
cards.back: Data visualisation means graphical or pictorial representation of the data using graph, chart, etc.
cards.quote: Data visualisation means graphical or pictorial representation of the data using graph, chart, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The purpose of plotting data is to visualise ____ or show ____ between variables.
cards.back: The purpose of plotting data is to visualise variation or show relationships between variables.
cards.quote: The purpose of plotting data is to visualise variation or show relationships between variables.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the Matplotlib library used for?
cards.back: Matplotlib library is used for creating static, animated, and interactive 2D- plots or figures in Python.
cards.quote: Matplotlib library is used for creating static, animated, and interactive 2D- plots or figures in Python.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Command to install Matplotlib from the command prompt.
cards.back: pip install matplotlib
cards.quote: pip install matplotlib

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Statement to import the Pyplot module for plotting.
cards.back: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
cards.quote: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The ____ module of matplotlib contains a collection of functions that can be used to work on a plot.
cards.back: The pyplot module of matplotlib contains a collection of functions that can be used to work on a plot.
cards.quote: The pyplot module of matplotlib contains a collection of functions that can be used to work on a plot.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a figure in pyplot?
cards.back: A figure is the overall window where the outputs of pyplot functions are plotted.
cards.quote: A figure is the overall window where the outputs of pyplot functions are plotted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which function of the pyplot module is used to create a figure?
cards.back: The plot() function of the pyplot module is used to create a figure.
cards.quote: The plot() function of the pyplot module is used to create a figure.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the parts a figure contains.
cards.back:
plotting area
legend
axis labels
ticks
title
cards.quote: A figure contains a plotting area, legend, axis labels, ticks, title, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How do we plot x versus y with pyplot?
cards.back: To plot x versus y, we can write plt.plot(x,y).
cards.quote: To plot x versus y, we can write plt.plot(x,y).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which function displays the figure created using plot()?
cards.back: The show() function is used to display the figure created using the plot() function.
cards.quote: The show() function is used to display the figure created using the plot() function.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What type of chart does the plot() function plot by default?
cards.back: As shown in Figure 4.2, the plot() function by default plots a line chart.
cards.quote: As shown in Figure 4.2, the plot() function by default plots a line chart.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which function saves a figure, and what is passed to it?
cards.back: A figure can also be saved by using savefig() function. The name of the figure is passed to the function as parameter.
cards.quote: A figure can also be saved by using savefig() function. The name of the figure is passed to the function as parameter.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Save the current figure under the name x.png.
cards.back: plt.savefig('x.png')
cards.quote: plt.savefig('x.png')

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Pyplot functions to plot different charts (Table 4.1).
cards.back:
plot(*args[, scalex, scaley, data])
Plot x versus y as lines and/or markers.
bar(x, height[, width, bottom, align, data])
Make a bar plot.
boxplot(x[, notch, sym, vert, whis, ...])
Make a box and whisker plot.
hist(x[, bins, range, density, weights, ...])
Plot a histogram.
pie(x[, explode, labels, colors, autopct, ...])
Plot a pie chart.
scatter(x, y[, s, c, marker, cmap, norm, ...])
A scatter plot of x versus y.
cards.quote: plot(*args[, scalex, scaley, data]) Plot x versus y as lines and/or markers. bar(x, height[, width, bottom, align, data]) Make a bar plot. boxplot(x[, notch, sym, vert, whis, ...]) Make a box and whisker plot. hist(x[, bins, range, density, weights, ...]) Plot a histogram. pie(x[, explode, labels, colors, autopct, ...]) Plot a pie chart. scatter(x, y[, s, c, marker, cmap, norm, ...]) A scatter plot of x versus y.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function makes a bar plot?
cards.back: bar(x, height[, width, bottom, align, data])
cards.quote: bar(x, height[, width, bottom, align, data]) Make a bar plot.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function makes a box and whisker plot?
cards.back: boxplot(x[, notch, sym, vert, whis, ...])
cards.quote: boxplot(x[, notch, sym, vert, whis, ...]) Make a box and whisker plot.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function plots a histogram?
cards.back: hist(x[, bins, range, density, weights, ...])
cards.quote: hist(x[, bins, range, density, weights, ...]) Plot a histogram.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function plots a pie chart?
cards.back: pie(x[, explode, labels, colors, autopct, ...])
cards.quote: pie(x[, explode, labels, colors, autopct, ...]) Plot a pie chart.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function makes a scatter plot of x versus y?
cards.back: scatter(x, y[, s, c, marker, cmap, norm, ...])
cards.quote: scatter(x, y[, s, c, marker, cmap, norm, ...]) A scatter plot of x versus y.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Pyplot functions to customise plots (Table 4.2).
cards.back:
grid([b, which, axis])
legend(*args, **kwargs)
savefig(*args, **kwargs)
show(*args, **kw)
title(label[, fontdict, loc, pad])
xlabel(xlabel[, fontdict, labelpad])
xticks([ticks, labels])
ylabel(ylabel[, fontdict, labelpad])
yticks([ticks, labels])
cards.quote: grid([b, which, axis]) Configure the grid lines. legend(*args, **kwargs) Place a legend on the axes. savefig(*args, **kwargs) Save the current figure. show(*args, **kw) Display all figures. title(label[, fontdict, loc, pad]) Set a title for the axes. xlabel(xlabel[, fontdict, labelpad]) Set the label for the x-axis. xticks([ticks, labels]) Get or set the current tick locations and labels of the x-axis. ylabel(ylabel[, fontdict, labelpad]) Set the label for the y-axis. yticks([ticks, labels]) Get or set the current tick locations and labels of the y-axis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function places a legend on the axes?
cards.back: legend(*args, **kwargs)
cards.quote: legend(*args, **kwargs) Place a legend on the axes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function sets a title for the axes?
cards.back: title(label[, fontdict, loc, pad])
cards.quote: title(label[, fontdict, loc, pad]) Set a title for the axes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function sets the label for the x-axis?
cards.back: xlabel(xlabel[, fontdict, labelpad])
cards.quote: xlabel(xlabel[, fontdict, labelpad]) Set the label for the x-axis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which pyplot function sets the label for the y-axis?
cards.back: ylabel(ylabel[, fontdict, labelpad])
cards.quote: ylabel(ylabel[, fontdict, labelpad]) Set the label for the y-axis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a marker in a plot?
cards.back: A marker is any symbol that represents a data value in a line chart or a scatter plot.
cards.quote: A marker is any symbol that represents a data value in a line chart or a scatter plot.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: We can either use ____ codes or the color names as values to the parameter color in the plot().
cards.back: We can either use character codes or the color names as values to the parameter color in the plot().
cards.quote: We can either use character codes or the color names as values to the parameter color in the plot().

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Colour abbreviations for plotting: b, g, r, c, m, y, k, w (Table 4.4).
cards.back:
b blue
g green
r red
c cyan
m magenta
y yellow
k black
w white
cards.quote: b blue g green r red c cyan m magenta y yellow k black w white

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The ____ and ____ property can be used to change the width and the style of the line chart.
cards.back: The linewidth and linestyle property can be used to change the width and the style of the line chart.
cards.quote: The linewidth and linestyle property can be used to change the width and the style of the line chart.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Linewidth is specified in ____.
cards.back: Linewidth is specified in pixels.
cards.quote: Linewidth is specified in pixels.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the default line width of a line chart?
cards.back: The default line width is 1 pixel showing a thin line.
cards.quote: The default line width is 1 pixel showing a thin line.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Strings the linestyle parameter can take.
cards.back:
solid
dotted
dashed
dashdot
cards.quote: It can take a string such as "solid", "dotted", "dashed" or "dashdot".

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Continuous data vs discrete data: the difference on how each is obtained.
cards.back: Continuous data are measured while discrete data are obtained by counting.
cards.quote: Continuous data are measured while discrete data are obtained by counting.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Height and weight versus the number of students in a class: which is continuous and which is discrete?
cards.back: Height, weight are examples of continuous data. It can be in decimals. Total number of students in a class is discrete. It can never be in decimals.
cards.quote: Height, weight are examples of continuous data. It can be in decimals. Total number of students in a class is discrete. It can never be in decimals.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: kind='bar' vs kind='barh': the plot each draws (Table 4.5).
cards.back: bar Vertical bar plot barh Horizontal bar plot
cards.quote: bar Vertical bar plot barh Horizontal bar plot

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Other values of kind besides line, bar and barh (Table 4.5).
cards.back:
hist
box
area
pie
scatter
cards.quote: hist box area pie scatter Histogram Boxplot Area plot Pie plot Scatter plot

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: General format of plotting a DataFrame.
cards.back: The general format of plotting a DataFrame is df.plot(kind = ' ') where df is the name of the DataFrame and kind can be line, bar, hist, scatter, box depending upon the type of plot to be displayed.
cards.quote: The general format of plotting a DataFrame is df.plot(kind = ' ') where df is the name of the DataFrame and kind can be line, bar, hist, scatter, box depending upon the type of plot to be displayed.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a line plot?
cards.back: A line plot is a graph that shows the frequency of data along a number line.
cards.quote: A line plot is a graph that shows the frequency of data along a number line.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A line plot is used to visualise ____ or ____ in data over a time interval.
cards.back: A line plot is used to visualise growth or decline in data over a time interval.
cards.quote: A line plot is used to visualise growth or decline in data over a time interval.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a Pandas line plot, what is displayed by default to associate colours with the plotted data?
cards.back: Note that the legend is displayed by default associating the colours with the plotted data.
cards.quote: Note that the legend is displayed by default associating the colours with the plotted data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The line plot takes a numeric value to display on the x axis and hence uses the ____ (row labels) of the DataFrame in the above example.
cards.back: The line plot takes a numeric value to display on the x axis and hence uses the index (row labels) of the DataFrame in the above example.
cards.quote: The line plot takes a numeric value to display on the x axis and hence uses the index (row labels) of the DataFrame in the above example.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How can we substitute the x-axis ticks with our own values (plt.xticks)?
cards.back: We can substitute the ticks at x axis with a list of values of our choice by using plt.xticks(ticks,label) where ticks is a list of locations(locs) on x axis at which ticks should be placed, label is a list of items to place at the given ticks.
cards.quote: We can substitute the ticks at x axis with a list of values of our choice by using plt.xticks(ticks,label) where ticks is a list of locations(locs) on x axis at which ticks should be placed, label is a list of items to place at the given ticks.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In order to show ____, we prefer Bar charts.
cards.back: In order to show comparisons, we prefer Bar charts.
cards.quote: In order to show comparisons, we prefer Bar charts.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Unlike line plots, bar charts can plot ____ on the x axis.
cards.back: Unlike line plots, bar charts can plot strings on the x axis.
cards.quote: Unlike line plots, bar charts can plot strings on the x axis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which kind value plots a bar chart?
cards.back: To plot a bar chart, we will specify kind='bar'.
cards.quote: To plot a bar chart, we will specify kind='bar'.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a DataFrame bar plot with no x column specified, what appears on the x axis?
cards.back: If we do not specify the column name for the x parameter in the plot(), the bar plot will plot all the columns of the DataFrame with the index (row label) of DataFrame at x axis which is a numeric starting from 0.
cards.quote: If we do not specify the column name for the x parameter in the plot(), the bar plot will plot all the columns of the DataFrame with the index (row label) of DataFrame at x axis which is a numeric starting from 0.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are histograms?
cards.back: Histograms are column-charts, where each column represents a range of values, and the height of a column corresponds to how many values are in that range.
cards.quote: Histograms are column-charts, where each column represents a range of values, and the height of a column corresponds to how many values are in that range.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: To make a histogram, the data is sorted into "____" and the number of data points in each bin is counted.
cards.back: To make a histogram, the data is sorted into "bins" and the number of data points in each bin is counted.
cards.quote: To make a histogram, the data is sorted into "bins" and the number of data points in each bin is counted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The height of each column in the histogram is then ____ to the number of data points its bin contains.
cards.back: The height of each column in the histogram is then proportional to the number of data points its bin contains.
cards.quote: The height of each column in the histogram is then proportional to the number of data points its bin contains.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does df.plot(kind='hist') choose the size of the bins?
cards.back: The df.plot(kind='hist') function automatically selects the size of the bins based on the spread of values in the data.
cards.quote: The df.plot(kind='hist') function automatically selects the size of the bins based on the spread of values in the data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are bins in a histogram?
cards.back: Bins are the number of intervals you want to divide all of your data into, such that it can be displayed as bars on a histogram.
cards.quote: Bins are the number of intervals you want to divide all of your data into, such that it can be displayed as bars on a histogram.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a histogram, what does the fill property do when True and when False?
cards.back: The default True means each hist will be filled with color and False means each hist will be empty.
cards.quote: The default True means each hist will be filled with color and False means each hist will be empty.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which histogram property fills each bar with a pattern?
cards.back: Another property called hatch can be used to fill to each hist with pattern ( '-', '+', 'x', '\\', '*', 'o', 'O', '.').
cards.quote: Another property called hatch can be used to fill to each hist with pattern ( '-', '+', 'x', '\\', '*', 'o', 'O', '.').

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a scatter chart?
cards.back: A scatter chart is a two-dimensional data visualisation method that uses dots to represent the values obtained for two different variables --one plotted along the x-axis and the other plotted along the y-axis.
cards.quote: A scatter chart is a two-dimensional data visualisation method that uses dots to represent the values obtained for two different variables --one plotted along the x-axis and the other plotted along the y-axis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Scatter plots are used when you want to show the ____ between two variables.
cards.back: Scatter plots are used when you want to show the relationship between two variables.
cards.quote: Scatter plots are used when you want to show the relationship between two variables.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Scatter plots are sometimes called ____ plots because they show how two variables are correlated.
cards.back: Scatter plots are sometimes called correlation plots because they show how two variables are correlated.
cards.quote: Scatter plots are sometimes called correlation plots because they show how two variables are correlated.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a scatter chart, what can the size, shape or colour of a dot represent?
cards.back: Additionally, the size, shape or color of the dot could represent a third (or even fourth variable).
cards.quote: Additionally, the size, shape or color of the dot could represent a third (or even fourth variable).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are quartiles?
cards.back: Quartiles are the measures which divide the data into four equal parts, and each part contains an equal number of observations.
cards.quote: Quartiles are the measures which divide the data into four equal parts, and each part contains an equal number of observations.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a box plot?
cards.back: A Box Plot is the visual representation of the statistical summary of a given data set.
cards.quote: A Box Plot is the visual representation of the statistical summary of a given data set.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are the whiskers of a box plot?
cards.back: The whiskers are the two lines outside the box that extend to the highest and lowest values.
cards.quote: The whiskers are the two lines outside the box that extend to the highest and lowest values.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is an outlier?
cards.back: An outlier is an observation that is numerically distant from the rest of the data
cards.quote: An outlier is an observation that is numerically distant from the rest of the data

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Pandas call to draw a box plot of a DataFrame.
cards.back: df.plot(kind='box')
cards.quote: df.plot(kind='box')

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Box plot whiskers: what does a shorter vs a longer distance indicate?
cards.back: Shorter distance indicates small variation in data, and longer distance indicates spread in data to mean larger variation.
cards.quote: Shorter distance indicates small variation in data, and longer distance indicates spread in data to mean larger variation.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which parameter displays the box plot whiskers in the horizontal direction?
cards.back: vert=False
cards.quote: We can display the whisker in horizontal direction by adding a parameter vert=False

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a pie chart?
cards.back: Pie is a type of graph in which a circle is divided into different sectors and each sector represents a part of the whole.
cards.quote: Pie is a type of graph in which a circle is divided into different sectors and each sector represents a part of the whole.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A pie plot is used to represent numerical data ____.
cards.back: A pie plot is used to represent numerical data proportionally.
cards.quote: A pie plot is used to represent numerical data proportionally.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What must be set to plot a pie chart with df.plot(kind='pie')?
cards.back: To plot a pie chart, either column label y or 'subplots=True' should be set while using df.plot(kind='pie').
cards.quote: To plot a pie chart, either column label y or 'subplots=True' should be set while using df.plot(kind='pie').

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: With no column given and subplots=True, what does a Pandas pie plot draw?
cards.back: If no column reference is passed and subplots=True, a 'pie' plot is drawn for each numerical column independently.
cards.quote: If no column reference is passed and subplots=True, a 'pie' plot is drawn for each numerical column independently.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a plot?
cards.back: A plot is a graphical representation of a data set which is also interchangeably known as a graph or chart.
cards.quote: A plot is a graphical representation of a data set which is also interchangeably known as a graph or chart.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The various components of a plot (Summary).
cards.back:
Title
Legend
Ticks
x label
ylabel
cards.quote: The various components of a plot are: Title, Legend, Ticks, x label, ylabel

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which functions set the x and y label of a plot?
cards.back: plt.xlabel() and plt.ylabel() are used to set the x and y label of the plot.
cards.quote: plt.xlabel() and plt.ylabel() are used to set the x and y label of the plot.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Queue?
cards.back: Queue is an ordered linear list of elements, having different ends for adding and removing elements in it.
cards.quote: Queue is an ordered linear list of elements, having different ends for adding and removing elements in it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Define the FIFO principle of a queue.
cards.back: Queue follows the principle of First In First Out (FIFO), since the element entering first in the queue will be the first one to come out of it.
cards.quote: Queue follows the principle of First In First Out (FIFO), since the element entering first in the queue will be the first one to come out of it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The FIFO principle of a queue is also known as which approach?
cards.back: It is also known as a First Come First Served (FCFS) approach.
cards.quote: It is also known as a First Come First Served (FCFS) approach.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does a queue add and remove items? What are the REAR and the FRONT?
cards.back: Queue is an arrangement in which new objects/items always get added at one end, usually called the REAR, and objects/items always get removed from the other end, usually called the FRONT of the queue.
cards.quote: Queue is an arrangement in which new objects/items always get added at one end, usually called the REAR, and objects/items always get removed from the other end, usually called the FRONT of the queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: REAR is also known as ____ and FRONT as ____ of a queue.
cards.back: REAR is also known as TAIL and FRONT as HEAD of a queue.
cards.quote: REAR is also known as TAIL and FRONT as HEAD of a queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a waiting-list queue of train tickets, from where is the W/L1 ticket removed when a confirmed ticket is cancelled?
cards.back: If a confirmed ticket is cancelled, the W/L1 numbered ticket is removed from the FRONT of the waiting queue and confirmed.
cards.quote: If a confirmed ticket is cancelled, the W/L1 numbered ticket is removed from the FRONT of the waiting queue and confirmed.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: On a customer service call, the Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) tells us to wait for a support person. Which concept is this?
cards.back: Sometimes on calling a customer service centre, the Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) tells us to wait till a support person is available. Here the call is put into a queue of customers waiting to be serviced.
cards.quote: Sometimes on calling a customer service centre, the Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) tells us to wait till a support person is available. Here the call is put into a queue of customers waiting to be serviced.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: On a single-lane one-way road, the vehicle that entered first exits first. Which concept is this?
cards.back: Imagine there is a single-lane one-way road, then the vehicle that entered first will exit first, following the concept of queue. Likewise, vehicles in a highway toll tax booth are served following the principle of FIFO.
cards.quote: Imagine there is a single-lane one-way road, then the vehicle that entered first will exit first, following the concept of queue. Likewise, vehicles in a highway toll tax booth are served following the principle of FIFO.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A web-server handles at most 50 concurrent requests but thousands of users want to view results. Which data structure suits?
cards.back: Suppose there is a web-server hosting a web-site to declare result(s). This server can handle a maximum of 50 concurrent requests to view result(s). So, to serve thousands of user requests, a Queue would be the most appropriate data structure to use.
cards.quote: Suppose there is a web-server hosting a web-site to declare result(s). This server can handle a maximum of 50 concurrent requests to view result(s). So, to serve thousands of user requests, a Queue would be the most appropriate data structure to use.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In a multitasking OS, how are jobs given access to the processor in the simplest way?
cards.back: in a multitasking operating system, jobs are lined up (queued) and then given access to the processor according to some order. The simplest way is to give access to the processor on a FIFO basis, that is according to the order in which the jobs arrive with a request for the processor.
cards.quote: in a multitasking operating system, jobs are lined up (queued) and then given access to the processor according to some order. The simplest way is to give access to the processor on a FIFO basis, that is according to the order in which the jobs arrive with a request for the processor.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Print commands arrive from multiple files or computers for a shared printer. How does the OS handle them?
cards.back: The OS puts these print requests in a queue and sends them to the printer one by one on a FIFO basis.
cards.quote: The OS puts these print requests in a queue and sends them to the printer one by one on a FIFO basis.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the ENQUEUE operation?
cards.back: ENQUEUE: is used to insert a new element to the queue at the rear end.
cards.quote: ENQUEUE: is used to insert a new element to the queue at the rear end.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Inserting elements beyond capacity of the queue will result in an exception - known as ____.
cards.back: Inserting elements beyond capacity of the queue will result in an exception - known as Overflow.
cards.quote: Inserting elements beyond capacity of the queue will result in an exception - known as Overflow.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the DEQUEUE operation?
cards.back: DEQUEUE: is used to remove one element at a time from the front of the queue.
cards.quote: DEQUEUE: is used to remove one element at a time from the front of the queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: We can delete elements from a queue until it is empty, trying to delete an element from an empty queue will result in exception - known as ____.
cards.back: We can delete elements from a queue until it is empty, trying to delete an element from an empty queue will result in exception - known as Underflow.
cards.quote: We can delete elements from a queue until it is empty, trying to delete an element from an empty queue will result in exception - known as Underflow.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the IS EMPTY operation on a queue?
cards.back: IS EMPTY : used to check whether the queue has any element or not, so as to avoid Underflow exception while performing dequeue operation.
cards.quote: IS EMPTY : used to check whether the queue has any element or not, so as to avoid Underflow exception while performing dequeue operation.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the PEEK operation on a queue?
cards.back: PEEK : used to view elements at the front of the queue, without removing it from the queue.
cards.quote: PEEK : used to view elements at the front of the queue, without removing it from the queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the IS FULL operation on a queue?
cards.back: IS FULL : used to check whether any more elements can be added to the queue or not, to avoid Overflow exceptions while performing enqueue operation.
cards.quote: IS FULL : used to check whether any more elements can be added to the queue or not, to avoid Overflow exceptions while performing enqueue operation.

cards.subject: computer_science

cards.back: There are many ways in which queues can be implemented in a computer program, one way is using the list data type of Python.
cards.quote: There are many ways in which queues can be implemented in a computer program, one way is using the list data type of Python.

myQueue = list()

cards.back: The function has two parameters - name of the queue and element which is to be inserted in the queue.
cards.quote: The function has two parameters - name of the queue and element which is to be inserted in the queue.

cards.back: append() function always adds an element at the end of the list, hence Rear of queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Why is Is Full not implemented for a queue made with a Python list?
cards.back: We don't need to implement Is Full, as Python being a dynamic language, does not ask for the creation of list having fixed size. Hence, we will never encounter a situation when the queue is full.

cards.back: It has one parameter - name of the queue and returns the deleted element.
cards.quote: It has one parameter - name of the queue and returns the deleted element.

cards.back: The pop() function with index[0] will delete the element from the beginning of the list, hence Front of queue.

cards.back: We can use the len() function of Python's list to find the number of elements in the queue.
