cards.back: The function has one parameter - name of the queue and returns the value of element at Front if queue is not empty, None otherwise.
cards.quote: The function has one parameter - name of the queue and returns the value of element at Front if queue is not empty, None otherwise.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Deque?
cards.back: Deque (pronounced as "deck") is an arrangement in which addition and removal of element(s) can happen from any end, i.e. head/front or tail/rear.
cards.quote: Deque (pronounced as "deck") is an arrangement in which addition and removal of element(s) can happen from any end, i.e. head/front or tail/rear.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: At a ticket counter, how may a person who already bought a ticket and returns with a query join the queue?
cards.back: As they have already purchased a ticket, they may have the privilege to join the queue from the front.
cards.quote: As they have already purchased a ticket, they may have the privilege to join the queue from the front.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: At a toll gate, what happens when all vehicles of one booth are served and its booth is vacant?
cards.back: In case all vehicles of a booth are served then vehicles from the other booth(s) are asked to form a queue in front of the vacant booth. So, vehicles at the end of those queues will leave (removed from the end from where queue was joined) current booth and join queue at the vacant booth.
cards.quote: In case all vehicles of a booth are served then vehicles from the other booth(s) are asked to form a queue in front of the vacant booth. cards.front: Why does browser history, usually kept as a stack, behave like a deque when the list of URLs becomes large?
cards.back: To maintain browser history (URL), usually a stack is used, because once a tab is closed and if you press ctrl+shift+T, the most recently closed URL is opened first. As the number of URLs which can be stored in history is fixed, so when this list of URLs becomes large, URLs from the end of the list (i.e. which were least visited) gets deleted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How is a string processed into a deque to check whether it is a palindrome?
cards.back: To check whether a given string is palindrome or not? Process string left to right (character wise) and insert it in deque from tail/rear like a normal queue.
cards.quote: To check whether a given string is palindrome or not? Process string left to right (character wise) and insert it in deque from tail/rear like a normal queue.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Once the whole string is in the deque, how is it checked for being a palindrome?
cards.back: Once the entire string is processed (i.e. inserted in deque) we will take out (delete) a character from both the ends and match them till there is no character left or only one character left in deque. In either case, string is palindrome.
cards.quote: Once the entire string is processed (i.e. inserted in deque) we will take out (delete) a character from both the ends and match them till there is no character left or only one character left in deque. In either case, string is palindrome.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the INSERTFRONT operation on a deque?
cards.back: INSERTFRONT: This operation is used to insert a new element at the front of the deque.
cards.quote: INSERTFRONT: This operation is used to insert a new element at the front of the deque.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the INSERTREAR operation on a deque?
cards.back: INSERTREAR: This operation is the same as a normal queue, i.e. insert a new element at the rear of the deque.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the DELETIONFRONT operation on a deque?
cards.back: DELETIONFRONT: This operation is the same as normal queue, i.e. to remove an element from the front of the deque.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the DELETIONREAR operation on a deque?
cards.back: DELETIONREAR: This operation is used to remove one element at a time from the rear of the deque.

Is Empty

Size

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Algorithm 4.1 (palindrome using a deque): Steps 1 to 3.
cards.back:
Step1: Start traversing string (madam) from left side, a character at a time.
Step 2: Insert the character in deque as normal queue using INSERTREAR.
Step 3: Repeat Step 1 and Step 2 for all characters of string (madam)
cards.quote: Step1: Start traversing string (madam) from left side, a character at a time. Step 2: Insert the character in deque as normal queue using INSERTREAR. Step 3: Repeat Step 1 and Step 2 for all characters of string (madam)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Algorithm 4.1, Step 4: what is removed from the deque, and with which operations?
cards.back: Step 4: Remove one character from the front and one character from the rear end of deque using DELETIONFRONT and DELETIONREAR we can do it.
cards.quote: Step 4: Remove one character from the front and one character from the rear end of deque using DELETIONFRONT and DELETIONREAR we can do it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Algorithm 4.1 (palindrome using a deque): Steps 5 and 6.
cards.back:
Step 5: Match these two removed characters.
Step 6: If they are same then repeat Step 4 and 5 till deque is empty or left with only one character, eventually string is Palindrome else stop as string is not palindrome
cards.quote: Step 5: Match these two removed characters. Step 6: If they are same then repeat Step 4 and 5 till deque is empty or left with only one character, eventually string is Palindrome else stop as string is not palindrome

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Linear search: how many comparisons are needed when the key is the first element of the list?
cards.back: Thus, if the key to be searched is the first element in the list, the linear search algorithm will always have to make only 1 comparison. This is the minimum amount of work that the linear search algorithm would have to do.
cards.quote: Thus, if the key to be searched is the first element in the list, the linear search algorithm will always have to make only 1 comparison. This is the minimum amount of work that the linear search algorithm would have to do.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Linear search: how many comparisons are needed when the key is the last element of the list?
cards.back: Thus, if the key to be searched is the last element in the list, the linear search algorithm will have to make n comparisons, where n is the number of elements in the list. This is in fact the maximum amount of work the linear search algorithm would have to do.
cards.quote: Thus, if the key to be searched is the last element in the list, the linear search algorithm will have to make n comparisons, where n is the number of elements in the list. This is in fact the maximum amount of work the linear search algorithm would have to do.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Linear search: how many comparisons are needed when the key is not present in the list?
cards.back: Thus, if the key is not present in the list, the linear search algorithm will have to make n comparisons. This again is a case where maximum work is done.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is binary search?
cards.back: The binary search is a search technique that makes use of the ordering of elements in the list to quickly search a key.
cards.quote: The binary search is a search technique that makes use of the ordering of elements in the list to quickly search a key.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For numeric values, the elements in the list may be arranged either in ____ or ____ order of their key values.
cards.back: For numeric values, the elements in the list may be arranged either in ascending or descending order of their key values.
cards.quote: For numeric values, the elements in the list may be arranged either in ascending or descending order of their key values.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In binary search the key is compared with the middle element of a sorted list. Name the three possibilities.
cards.back:
i) the element at the middle position itself matches the key or
ii) the element at the middle position is greater than the key or
iii) the element at the middle position is smaller than the key
cards.quote: In binary search, the key to be searched is compared with the element in the middle of a sorted list. This could result in either of the three possibilities: i) the element at the middle position itself matches the key or ii) the element at the middle position is greater than the key or iii) the element at the middle position is smaller than the key

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Why does NCERT use the term iteration and not comparison in binary search?
cards.back: We are using the term iteration and not comparison in binary search, because after every unsuccessful comparison, we change the search area redefining the first, mid and last position before making subsequent comparisons.
cards.quote: We are using the term iteration and not comparison in binary search, because after every unsuccessful comparison, we change the search area redefining the first, mid and last position before making subsequent comparisons.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What condition must the list satisfy for binary search to work?
cards.back: That is, the list needs to be sorted.
cards.quote: Thus, it is evident that unlike linear search of elements one-by-one, we can search more efficiently using binary search provided the list from which we want to search is arranged in some order. That is, the list needs to be sorted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Binary search: how is mid calculated for a list with an even number of elements? Give the 10-element case.
cards.back: If the list to be searched contains an even number of elements, the mid value is calculated using the floor division (//) operator. If there are 10 elements in the list, then the middle position (mid) = 10//2 = 5.
cards.quote: If the list to be searched contains an even number of elements, the mid value is calculated using the floor division (//) operator. If there are 10 elements in the list, then the middle position (mid) = 10//2 = 5.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Steps of Algorithm 6.2 (Binary Search), in order.
cards.back:
Step 1: SET first = 0, last = n-1
Step 2: Calculate mid = (first+last)//2
Step 3: WHILE first <= last REPEAT Step 4
Step 4: IF numList[mid] = key PRINT "Element found at position", mid+1 STOP ELSE IF numList[mid] > key, THEN last = mid-1 ELSE first = mid + 1
Step 5: PRINT "Search unsuccessful"
cards.quote: Step 1: SET first = 0, last = n-1 Step 2: Calculate mid = (first+last)//2 Step 3: WHILE first <= last REPEAT Step 4 Step 4: IF numList[mid] = key PRINT "Element found at position", mid+1 STOP ELSE IF numList[mid] > key, THEN last = mid-1 ELSE first = mid + 1 Step 5: PRINT "Search unsuccessful"

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Does binary search change the list? What changes in each iteration?
cards.back: The binary search algorithm does not change the list. Rather, after every pass of the algorithm, the search area gets reduced by half. That is, only the index of the element to be compared with the key changes in each iteration.
cards.quote: The binary search algorithm does not change the list. Rather, after every pass of the algorithm, the search area gets reduced by half. That is, only the index of the element to be compared with the key changes in each iteration.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Binary search: when is only 1 iteration required?
cards.back: Thus, binary search requires only 1 iteration when the key to be searched is the middle value in the list.
cards.quote: Thus, binary search requires only 1 iteration when the key to be searched is the middle value in the list.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Binary search for key 2 in the sorted 15-element numList [2, 3, 5, ... 43]: how many iterations?
cards.back: As we can see, the binary search algorithm had to make 4 iterations to narrow down the list to a single element and decide that the search key is the first element of list. This is clearly the maximum work required to find a key in the given list.
cards.quote: As we can see, the binary search algorithm had to make 4 iterations to narrow down the list to a single element and decide that the search key is the first element of list. This is clearly the maximum work required to find a key in the given list.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is hashing?
cards.back: Hashing is a technique which can be used to know the presence of a key in a list in just one step.
cards.quote: Hashing is a technique which can be used to know the presence of a key in a list in just one step.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a hash function?
cards.back: A formula called hash function is used to calculate the value at an index in the list.
cards.quote: A formula called hash function is used to calculate the value at an index in the list.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a hash function do, and what is the new list it generates called?
cards.back: Thus, a hash function takes elements of a list one by one and generates an index value for every element. This will generate a new list called the hash table.
cards.quote: Thus, a hash function takes elements of a list one by one and generates an index value for every element. This will generate a new list called the hash table.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Each index of the hash table can hold ____ and the positions are indexed by integer values starting from 0.
cards.back: Each index of the hash table can hold only one item and the positions are indexed by integer values starting from 0.
cards.quote: Each index of the hash table can hold only one item and the positions are indexed by integer values starting from 0.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the remainder method of hashing, and what is the remainder called?
cards.back: A simple hash function that works with numeric values is known as the remainder method. It takes an element from a list and divides it by the size of the hash table. The remainder so generated is called the hash value.
cards.quote: A simple hash function that works with numeric values is known as the remainder method. It takes an element from a list and divides it by the size of the hash table. The remainder so generated is called the hash value.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Formula: hash function by the remainder method.
cards.back: It takes an element from a list and divides it by the size of the hash table. The remainder so generated is called the hash value. h(element) = element % size(hash table)
cards.quote: It takes an element from a list and divides it by the size of the hash table. The remainder so generated is called the hash value. h(element) = element % size(hash table)

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How do you search for a key using a hash table?
cards.back: Now, to search for a key, we can calculate its index using the hashing function and compare the element at that index with the key to declare whether the element is present in the list or not.
cards.quote: Now, to search for a key, we can calculate its index using the hashing function and compare the element at that index with the key to declare whether the element is present in the list or not.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: We must have a mechanism for placing the other items with the same hash value in the hash table. This process is called ____.
cards.back: We must have a mechanism for placing the other items with the same hash value in the hash table. This process is called collision resolution.
cards.quote: We must have a mechanism for placing the other items with the same hash value in the hash table. This process is called collision resolution.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a perfect hash function?
cards.back: If every item of the list maps to a unique index in the hash table, the hash function is called a perfect hash function. If a hash function is perfect, collision will never occur.
cards.quote: If every item of the list maps to a unique index in the hash table, the hash function is called a perfect hash function. If a hash function is perfect, collision will never occur.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Apart from the modulo division method, name techniques on which hash functions may be based.
cards.back:
integer division
shift folding
boundary folding
mid-square function
extraction
radix transformation
cards.quote: Apart from modulo division method, hash functions may be based on several other techniques like integer division, shift folding, boundary folding, mid-square function, extraction, radix transformation, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The advantage of hashing is that the time required to compute the index value is ____ of the number of items in the search list.
cards.back: The advantage of hashing is that the time required to compute the index value is independent of the number of items in the search list.
cards.quote: The advantage of hashing is that the time required to compute the index value is independent of the number of items in the search list.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Linear search checks the elements of a list, ____, without skipping any element.
cards.back: Linear search checks the elements of a list, one at a time, without skipping any element.
cards.quote: Linear search checks the elements of a list, one at a time, without skipping any element.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Summary: when is linear search useful, and when is it slow and time-consuming?
cards.back: It is useful when we need to search for an item in a small unsorted list, but it is slow and time-consuming when the list contains a large number of items.
cards.quote: It is useful when we need to search for an item in a small unsorted list, but it is slow and time-consuming when the list contains a large number of items.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is collision in hashing?
cards.back: When two elements map to the same slot in the hash table, it is called collision.
cards.quote: When two elements map to the same slot in the hash table, it is called collision.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is collision resolution?
cards.back: The process of identifying a slot for the second and further items in the hash table in the event of collision, is called collision resolution.
cards.quote: The process of identifying a slot for the second and further items in the hash table in the event of collision, is called collision resolution.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is network security?
cards.back: Network security is concerned with protection of our device as well as data from illegitimate access or misuse.
cards.quote: Network security is concerned with protection of our device as well as data from illegitimate access or misuse.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What do threats include, in network security?
cards.back: Threats include all the ways in which one can exploit any vulnerability or weakness in a network or communication system in order to cause harm or damage one's reputation.
cards.quote: Threats include all the ways in which one can exploit any vulnerability or weakness in a network or communication system in order to cause harm or damage one's reputation.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is malware?
cards.back: Malware is a short term used for MALicious softWARE. It is any software developed with an intention to damage hardware devices, steal data, or cause any other trouble to the user.
cards.quote: Malware is a short term used for MALicious softWARE. It is any software developed with an intention to damage hardware devices, steal data, or cause any other trouble to the user.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who coined the term computer virus, and in which year?
cards.back: The term computer virus was coined by Fred Cohen in 1985 and has been borrowed from biological science with almost similar meaning and behavior, the only difference is that the victim is a computer system and the virus is a malicious software.
cards.quote: The term computer virus was coined by Fred Cohen in 1985 and has been borrowed from biological science with almost similar meaning and behavior, the only difference is that the victim is a computer system and the virus is a malicious software.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a computer virus?
cards.back: A virus is a piece of software code created to perform malicious activities and hamper resources of a computer system like CPU time, memory, personal files, or sensitive information.
cards.quote: A virus is a piece of software code created to perform malicious activities and hamper resources of a computer system like CPU time, memory, personal files, or sensitive information.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does a computer virus infect other systems?
cards.back: a computer virus infects other computer systems that it comes into contact with by copying or inserting its code into the computer programs or software (executable files).
cards.quote: a computer virus infects other computer systems that it comes into contact with by copying or inserting its code into the computer programs or software (executable files).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: A virus remains ____ on a system and is activated as soon as the infected file is opened (executed) by a user.
cards.back: A virus remains dormant on a system and is activated as soon as the infected file is opened (executed) by a user.
cards.quote: A virus remains dormant on a system and is activated as soon as the infected file is opened (executed) by a user.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the common motives behind viruses.
cards.back:
stealing passwords or data
corrupting files
spamming the user's email contacts
taking control of the user's machine
cards.quote: Some of the most common intentions or motives behind viruses include stealing passwords or data, corrupting files, spamming the user's email contacts, and even taking control of the user's machine.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name some well-known computer viruses.
cards.back: Some well-known viruses include CryptoLocker, ILOVEYOU, MyDoom, Sasser and Netsky, Slammer, Stuxnet, etc.
cards.quote: Some well-known viruses include CryptoLocker, ILOVEYOU, MyDoom, Sasser and Netsky, Slammer, Stuxnet, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a worm?
cards.back: The Worm is also a malware that incurs unexpected or damaging behaviour on an infected computer system.
cards.quote: The Worm is also a malware that incurs unexpected or damaging behaviour on an infected computer system.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Worm vs virus: the difference on needing a host program.
cards.back: The major difference between a worm and a virus is that unlike a virus, a worm does not need a host program or software to insert its code into. Worms are standalone programs that are capable of working on its own.
cards.quote: The major difference between a worm and a virus is that unlike a virus, a worm does not need a host program or software to insert its code into. Worms are standalone programs that are capable of working on its own.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Worm vs virus: the difference on how each replicates.
cards.back: Also, a virus needs human triggering for replication (i.e. when a user opens/executes the infected file), while a worm replicates on its own and can spread to other computers through the network.
cards.quote: Also, a virus needs human triggering for replication (i.e. when a user opens/executes the infected file), while a worm replicates on its own and can spread to other computers through the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How did the Trojan malware get its name?
cards.back: Since the ancient Greeks could not infiltrate the city of Troy using traditional warfare methods, they gifted the king of Troy with a big wooden horse with hidden soldiers inside and eventually defeated them.
cards.quote: Since the ancient Greeks could not infiltrate the city of Troy using traditional warfare methods, they gifted the king of Troy with a big wooden horse with hidden soldiers inside and eventually defeated them.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Some Trojans create ____ to give malicious users access to the system.
cards.back: Some Trojans create backdoors to give malicious users access to the system.
cards.quote: Some Trojans create backdoors to give malicious users access to the system.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is adware?
cards.back: An Adware is a malware that is created to generate revenue for its developer. An adware displays online advertisements using pop-ups, web pages, or installation screens.
cards.quote: An Adware is a malware that is created to generate revenue for its developer. An adware displays online advertisements using pop-ups, web pages, or installation screens.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does adware generate revenue for its developer?
cards.back: Once an adware has infected a substantial number of computer systems, it generates revenue either by displaying advertisements or using "pay per click" mechanism to charge its clients against the number of clicks on their displayed ads.
cards.quote: Once an adware has infected a substantial number of computer systems, it generates revenue either by displaying advertisements or using "pay per click" mechanism to charge its clients against the number of clicks on their displayed ads.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Adware is usually annoying, but ____. However, it often paves way for other malware by displaying unsafe links as advertisements.
cards.back: Adware is usually annoying, but harmless. However, it often paves way for other malware by displaying unsafe links as advertisements.
cards.quote: Adware is usually annoying, but harmless. However, it often paves way for other malware by displaying unsafe links as advertisements.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the common routes by which malware reaches a computer.
cards.back:
Downloaded from the Internet
Spam Email
Removable Storage Devices
network propagation
cards.quote: A malware can take many routes to reach your computer, which include: Downloaded from the Internet, Spam Email, using infected Removable Storage Devices, and network propagation.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does replicating malware use removable storage devices to spread?
cards.back: Often, the replicating malware targets the removable storage media like pen drives, SSD cards, music players, mobile phones, etc. and infect them with malware that gets transferred to other systems that they are plugged into.
cards.quote: Often, the replicating malware targets the removable storage media like pen drives, SSD cards, music players, mobile phones, etc. and infect them with malware that gets transferred to other systems that they are plugged into.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Some malware like ____ have the ability to propagate from one computer to another through a network connection.
cards.back: Some malware like Worms have the ability to propagate from one computer to another through a network connection.
cards.quote: Some malware like Worms have the ability to propagate from one computer to another through a network connection.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name common signs of malware infection.
cards.back:
frequent pop-up windows prompting you to visit some website and/or download some software
changes to the default homepage of your web browser
mass emails being sent from your email account
unusually slow computer with frequent crashes
unknown programs startup as you turn on your computer
programs opening and closing automatically
sudden lack of storage space, random messages, sounds, or music start to appear
programs or files appear or disappear without your knowledge
cards.quote: Common signs of some malware infection include the following: frequent pop-up windows prompting you to visit some website and/or download some software; changes to the default homepage of your web browser; mass emails being sent from your email account; unusually slow computer with frequent crashes; unknown programs startup as you turn on your computer; programs opening and closing automatically; sudden lack of storage space, random messages, sounds, or music start to appear; programs or files appear or disappear without your knowledge.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Do not install an anti-spyware or antivirus program presented to you in a ____ or ad.
cards.back: Do not install an anti-spyware or antivirus program presented to you in a pop-up or ad.
cards.quote: Do not install an anti-spyware or antivirus program presented to you in a pop-up or ad.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a virus signature?
cards.back: A virus signature is a consecutive sequence of bytes that is commonly found in a certain malware sample. That means it's contained within the malware or the infected file and not in unaffected files.
cards.quote: A virus signature is a consecutive sequence of bytes that is commonly found in a certain malware sample. That means it's contained within the malware or the infected file and not in unaffected files.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is antivirus software?
cards.back: Antivirus is a software, also known as anti-malware. Initially, antivirus software was developed to detect and remove viruses only and hence the name antivirus.
cards.quote: Antivirus is a software, also known as anti-malware. Initially, antivirus software was developed to detect and remove viruses only and hence the name antivirus.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In this method, an antivirus works with the help of a signature database known as "____".
cards.back: In this method, an antivirus works with the help of a signature database known as "Virus Definition File (VDF)".
cards.quote: In this method, an antivirus works with the help of a signature database known as "Virus Definition File (VDF)".

source.section: 12.3.1 Methods of Malware Identification used by Antivirus

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Some malware remains dormant or gets activated after some time. Such malware needs to be checked on a ____ basis.
cards.back: Some malware remains dormant or gets activated after some time. Such malware needs to be checked on a real-time basis.
cards.quote: Some malware remains dormant or gets activated after some time. Such malware needs to be checked on a real-time basis.

source.section: 12.3.1 Methods of Malware Identification used by Antivirus

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does real-time protection work in an antivirus?
cards.back: In this technique, the anti-malware software keeps running in the background and observes the behavior of an application or file for any suspicious activity while it is being executed i.e. when it resides in the active (main) memory of the computer system.
cards.quote: In this technique, the anti-malware software keeps running in the background and observes the behavior of an application or file for any suspicious activity while it is being executed i.e. when it resides in the active (main) memory of the computer system.

source.section: 12.3.1 Methods of Malware Identification used by Antivirus

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is spam?
cards.back: Any unwanted data, information, email, advertisement, etc. is called Spam.
cards.quote: Any unwanted data, information, email, advertisement, etc. is called Spam.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Which is the widely recognised form of spam?
cards.back: Spam is a broad term and applies to various digital platforms like messaging, forums, chatting, emailing, advertisement, etc. However, the widely recognised form is email spam.
cards.quote: Spam is a broad term and applies to various digital platforms like messaging, forums, chatting, emailing, advertisement, etc. However, the widely recognised form is email spam.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How do organisations or individuals send email spam?
cards.back: Depending on their requirements, organisations or individuals buy or create a mailing list (list of email addresses) and repeatedly send advertisement links and invitation emails to a large number of users.
cards.quote: Depending on their requirements, organisations or individuals buy or create a mailing list (list of email addresses) and repeatedly send advertisement links and invitation emails to a large number of users.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How can a user stop an undetected unsolicited email from reaching the inbox in future?
cards.back: A user can also mark an undetected unsolicited email as "spam", thereby ensuring that such type of email is not delivered into the inbox as normal email in future.
cards.quote: A user can also mark an undetected unsolicited email as "spam", thereby ensuring that such type of email is not delivered into the inbox as normal email in future.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are HTTP and HTTPS?
cards.back: Both the HTTP (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol) and its variant HTTPS (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol Secure) are a set of rules (protocol) that govern how data can be transmitted over the WWW (World Wide Web).
cards.quote: Both the HTTP (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol) and its variant HTTPS (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol Secure) are a set of rules (protocol) that govern how data can be transmitted over the WWW (World Wide Web).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: HTTPS encrypts the data before transmission. At the receiver end, it ____ to recover the original data.
cards.back: HTTPS encrypts the data before transmission. At the receiver end, it decrypts to recover the original data.
cards.quote: HTTPS encrypts the data before transmission. At the receiver end, it decrypts to recover the original data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The HTTPS based websites require ____.
cards.back: The HTTPS based websites require SSL Digital Certificate.
cards.quote: The HTTPS based websites require SSL Digital Certificate.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For which kinds of websites is HTTP sufficient?
cards.back: Hence, HTTP is sufficient for websites with public information sharing like news portals, blogs, etc.
cards.quote: Hence, HTTP is sufficient for websites with public information sharing like news portals, blogs, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a firewall?
cards.back: Computer firewall is a network security system designed to protect a trusted private network from unauthorised access or traffic originating from an untrusted outside network (e.g., the Internet or different sections of the same network) to which it is connected
cards.quote: Computer firewall is a network security system designed to protect a trusted private network from unauthorised access or traffic originating from an untrusted outside network (e.g., the Internet or different sections of the same network) to which it is connected

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Firewall can be implemented in software, ____ or both.
cards.back: Firewall can be implemented in software, hardware or both.
cards.quote: Firewall can be implemented in software, hardware or both.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Example: what rule can a school LAN firewall enforce about the finance server?
cards.back: As an example, a rule can be set in the firewall of a school LAN, that a student cannot access data from the finance server, while the school accountant can access the finance server.
cards.quote: As an example, a rule can be set in the firewall of a school LAN, that a student cannot access data from the finance server, while the school accountant can access the finance server.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Types of firewall.
cards.back:
Network Firewall
Host-based Firewall
cards.quote: There are two basic types of firewalls - Network Firewall and Host-based Firewall.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Network Firewall?
cards.back: If the firewall is placed between two or more networks and monitors the network traffic between different networks, it is termed as Network Firewall.
cards.quote: If the firewall is placed between two or more networks and monitors the network traffic between different networks, it is termed as Network Firewall.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Host-based Firewall?
cards.back: If the firewall is placed on a computer and monitors the network traffic to and from that computer, it is called a host-based firewall.
cards.quote: If the firewall is placed on a computer and monitors the network traffic to and from that computer, it is called a host-based firewall.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a computer cookie?
cards.back: A computer cookie is a small file or data packet, which is stored by a website on the client's computer.
cards.quote: A computer cookie is a small file or data packet, which is stored by a website on the client's computer.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Example: how does an e-commerce site remember the items a user adds to the cart?
cards.back: For example, while going through an e-commerce website, when a user adds items to cart, the website usually uses cookies to record the items in the cart.
cards.quote: For example, while going through an e-commerce website, when a user adds items to cart, the website usually uses cookies to record the items in the cart.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name user-centric information a cookie can store.
cards.back:
login credentials
language preference
search queries
recently viewed web pages
music choice
favorite cuisine
cards.quote: A cookie can also be used to store other user-centric information like login credentials, language preference, search queries, recently viewed web pages, music choice, favorite cuisine, etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____ keep track of the current session and even terminate the session when there is a time-out (banking website).
cards.back: Session cookies keep track of the current session and even terminate the session when there is a time-out (banking website).
cards.quote: Session cookies keep track of the current session and even terminate the session when there is a time-out (banking website).

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Similarly, ____ are used by a website to check if the user is previously logged in (authenticated) or not.
cards.back: Similarly, authentication cookies are used by a website to check if the user is previously logged in (authenticated) or not.
cards.quote: Similarly, authentication cookies are used by a website to check if the user is previously logged in (authenticated) or not.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: There is another type of cookie known as "____" that gets recreated after being deleted.
cards.back: There is another type of cookie known as "Zombie cookie" that gets recreated after being deleted.
cards.quote: There is another type of cookie known as "Zombie cookie" that gets recreated after being deleted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Some ____ cookies might share user data without the consent of the user for advertising or tracking purposes.
cards.back: Some third-party cookies might share user data without the consent of the user for advertising or tracking purposes.
cards.quote: Some third-party cookies might share user data without the consent of the user for advertising or tracking purposes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a hacktivist?
cards.back: A hacktivist is a hacker with an aim to bring about political and social change.
cards.quote: A hacktivist is a hacker with an aim to bring about political and social change.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who are hackers and crackers?
cards.back: Hackers and crackers are people having a thorough knowledge of the computer systems, system software (operating system), computer networks, and programming. They use this knowledge to find loopholes and vulnerabilities in computer systems or computer networks and gain access to unauthorised information.
cards.quote: Hackers and crackers are people having a thorough knowledge of the computer systems, system software (operating system), computer networks, and programming. They use this knowledge to find loopholes and vulnerabilities in computer systems or computer networks and gain access to unauthorised information.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a hacker, in simple terms?
cards.back: In simple terms, a hacker is a person that is skilled enough to hack or take control of a computer system.
cards.quote: In simple terms, a hacker is a person that is skilled enough to hack or take control of a computer system.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who is a White Hat hacker?
cards.back: If a hacker uses its knowledge to find and help in fixing the security flaws in the system, its termed as White Hat hacker.
cards.quote: If a hacker uses its knowledge to find and help in fixing the security flaws in the system, its termed as White Hat hacker.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Organisations hire ____ or white hat hackers to check and fix their systems for potential security threats and loopholes.
cards.back: Organisations hire ethical or white hat hackers to check and fix their systems for potential security threats and loopholes.
cards.quote: Organisations hire ethical or white hat hackers to check and fix their systems for potential security threats and loopholes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Technically, white hats work ____ black hats.
cards.back: Technically, white hats work against black hats.
cards.quote: Technically, white hats work against black hats.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who is a Black Hat hacker?
cards.back: If hackers use their knowledge unethically to break the law and disrupt security by exploiting the flaws and loopholes in a system, then they are called black hat hackers.
cards.quote: If hackers use their knowledge unethically to break the law and disrupt security by exploiting the flaws and loopholes in a system, then they are called black hat hackers.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who is a Grey Hat hacker?
cards.back: The distinction between different hackers is not always clear. There exists a grey area in between, which represents the class of hackers that are neutral, they hack systems by exploiting its vulnerabilities, but they don't do so for monetary or political gains.
cards.quote: The distinction between different hackers is not always clear. There exists a grey area in between, which represents the class of hackers that are neutral, they hack systems by exploiting its vulnerabilities, but they don't do so for monetary or political gains.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The grey hats take system security as a ____ and just hack systems for the fun of it.
cards.back: The grey hats take system security as a challenge and just hack systems for the fun of it.
cards.quote: The grey hats take system security as a challenge and just hack systems for the fun of it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Denial of Service (DoS) attack?
cards.back: Denial of Service (DoS) is a scenario, wherein an attacker (Hacker) limits or stops an authorised user to access a service, device, or any such resource by overloading that resource with illegitimate requests.
cards.quote: Denial of Service (DoS) is a scenario, wherein an attacker (Hacker) limits or stops an authorised user to access a service, device, or any such resource by overloading that resource with illegitimate requests.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How do attackers carry out a DoS attack on a website?
cards.back: If attackers carry out a DoS attack on a website, they will flood it with a very large number of network packets by using different IP addresses.
cards.quote: If attackers carry out a DoS attack on a website, they will flood it with a very large number of network packets by using different IP addresses.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack?
cards.back: A variant of DoS, known as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) is an attack, where the flooded requests come from compromised computer (Zombies) systems distributed across the globe or over a very large area.
cards.quote: A variant of DoS, known as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) is an attack, where the flooded requests come from compromised computer (Zombies) systems distributed across the globe or over a very large area.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The attacker installs a malicious software known as ____ on the Zombie machines, which gives it control over these machines.
cards.back: The attacker installs a malicious software known as Bot on the Zombie machines, which gives it control over these machines.
cards.quote: The attacker installs a malicious software known as Bot on the Zombie machines, which gives it control over these machines.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: DoS vs DDoS: the difference in how each can be countered.
cards.back: While as a simple DoS attack may be countered by blocking requests or network packets from a single source, DDoS is very difficult to resolve, as the attack is carried from multiple distributed locations.
cards.quote: While as a simple DoS attack may be countered by blocking requests or network packets from a single source, DDoS is very difficult to resolve, as the attack is carried from multiple distributed locations.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is network intrusion?
cards.back: Network Intrusion refers to any unauthorised activity on a computer network.
cards.quote: Network Intrusion refers to any unauthorised activity on a computer network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is the asymmetric routing intrusion attack?
cards.back: The attacker tends to avoid detection by sending the intrusion packets through multiple paths, thereby bypassing the network intrusion sensors.
cards.quote: The attacker tends to avoid detection by sending the intrusion packets through multiple paths, thereby bypassing the network intrusion sensors.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a buffer overflow attack?
cards.back: In this attack, the attacker overwrites certain memory areas of the computers within the network with code (set of commands) that will be executed later when the buffer overflow (programming error) occurs. Once the malicious code is executed, an attacker can initiate a DoS attack or gain access to the network.
cards.quote: In this attack, the attacker overwrites certain memory areas of the computers within the network with code (set of commands) that will be executed later when the buffer overflow (programming error) occurs. Once the malicious code is executed, an attacker can initiate a DoS attack or gain access to the network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is traffic flooding, as a network intrusion method?
cards.back: It is one of the most trivial methods of network intrusion. It involves flooding the network intrusion detection system with message packets.
cards.quote: It is one of the most trivial methods of network intrusion. It involves flooding the network intrusion detection system with message packets.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is snooping?
cards.back: Snooping means secretly listening to a conversation. In the context of networking, it refers to the process of secret capture and analysis of network traffic.
cards.quote: Snooping means secretly listening to a conversation. In the context of networking, it refers to the process of secret capture and analysis of network traffic.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Snooping is also known as ____.
cards.back: Snooping is also known as Sniffing.
cards.quote: Snooping is also known as Sniffing.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What function do various network hubs and switches have for snooping?
cards.back: Besides, various network hubs and switches have a SPAN (Sniffer Port Analyser) port function for snooping.
cards.quote: Besides, various network hubs and switches have a SPAN (Sniffer Port Analyser) port function for snooping.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: In older days, eavesdropping was performed on the conventional telephone line and was known as ____.
cards.back: In older days, eavesdropping was performed on the conventional telephone line and was known as wiretapping.
cards.quote: In older days, eavesdropping was performed on the conventional telephone line and was known as wiretapping.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Digital devices like laptops and cell phones that have a built-in microphone or camera can be easily hacked and eavesdropped using ____ malware.
cards.back: Digital devices like laptops and cell phones that have a built-in microphone or camera can be easily hacked and eavesdropped using rootkit malware.
cards.quote: Digital devices like laptops and cell phones that have a built-in microphone or camera can be easily hacked and eavesdropped using rootkit malware.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Snooping vs eavesdropping: the difference on storing the traffic.
cards.back: Unlike snooping, where the network traffic can be stored for later analysis, eavesdropping is an unauthorised real-time interception or monitoring of private communication between two entities over a network.
cards.quote: Unlike snooping, where the network traffic can be stored for later analysis, eavesdropping is an unauthorised real-time interception or monitoring of private communication between two entities over a network.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Snooping vs eavesdropping: the difference on timing.
cards.back: Eavesdropping is different from Snooping. While the former happens in real time, the latter does not.
cards.quote: Eavesdropping is different from Snooping. While the former happens in real time, the latter does not.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a digital footprint?
cards.back: Whenever we surf the Internet using smartphones, tablets, computers, etc., we leave a trail of data reflecting the activities performed by us online, which is our digital footprint.
cards.quote: Whenever we surf the Internet using smartphones, tablets, computers, etc., we leave a trail of data reflecting the activities performed by us online, which is our digital footprint.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are active digital footprints?
cards.back: Active digital footprints which includes data that we intentionally submit online.
cards.quote: Active digital footprints which includes data that we intentionally submit online.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are passive digital footprints?
cards.back: The digital data trail we leave online unintentionally is called passive digital footprints.
cards.quote: The digital data trail we leave online unintentionally is called passive digital footprints.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Besides browser, most of our digital footprints are stored in ____ where the applications are hosted.
cards.back: Besides browser, most of our digital footprints are stored in servers where the applications are hosted.
cards.quote: Besides browser, most of our digital footprints are stored in servers where the applications are hosted.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: There is ____ that digital footprints will be fully eliminated from the Internet.
cards.back: There is no guarantee that digital footprints will be fully eliminated from the Internet.
cards.quote: There is no guarantee that digital footprints will be fully eliminated from the Internet.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: But remember, it cannot be permanently deleted. It is recorded in our ____.
cards.back: But remember, it cannot be permanently deleted. It is recorded in our Digital Footprint.
cards.quote: But remember, it cannot be permanently deleted. It is recorded in our Digital Footprint.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____ thus reflects the growing trend of using digital technologies in all spheres of human activities.
cards.back: Digital society thus reflects the growing trend of using digital technologies in all spheres of human activities.
cards.quote: Digital society thus reflects the growing trend of using digital technologies in all spheres of human activities.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who is a digital citizen or netizen?
cards.back: Anyone who uses digital technology along with Internet is a digital citizen or a netizen.
cards.quote: Anyone who uses digital technology along with Internet is a digital citizen or a netizen.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does being a good netizen mean?
cards.back: Being a good netizen means practicing safe, ethical and legal use of digital technology.
cards.quote: Being a good netizen means practicing safe, ethical and legal use of digital technology.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the three kinds of etiquettes a responsible netizen must abide by.
cards.back:
net etiquettes
communication etiquettes
social media etiquettes
cards.quote: A responsible netizen must abide by net etiquettes, communication etiquettes and social media etiquettes.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Net etiquette, Be Ethical: what about copyrighted materials?
cards.back: No copyright violation: we should not use copyrighted materials without the permission of the creator or owner.
cards.quote: No copyright violation: we should not use copyrighted materials without the permission of the creator or owner.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: ____: it is good to share information and knowledge on Internet so that others can access it.
cards.back: Share the expertise: it is good to share information and knowledge on Internet so that others can access it.
cards.quote: Share the expertise: it is good to share information and knowledge on Internet so that others can access it.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: We should respect this privacy and should not share those images, documents, files, etc., with any other digital citizen without each others' ____.
cards.back: We should respect this privacy and should not share those images, documents, files, etc., with any other digital citizen without each others' consent.
cards.quote: We should respect this privacy and should not share those images, documents, files, etc., with any other digital citizen without each others' consent.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is cyber bullying?
cards.back: any insulting, degrading or intimidating online behaviour like repeated posting of rumours, giving threats online, posting the victim's personal information, sexual harassment or comments aimed to publicly ridicule a victim is termed as cyber bullying.
cards.quote: any insulting, degrading or intimidating online behaviour like repeated posting of rumours, giving threats online, posting the victim's personal information, sexual harassment or comments aimed to publicly ridicule a victim is termed as cyber bullying.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Who is an Internet troll?
cards.back: an Internet troll is a person who deliberately sows discord on the Internet by starting quarrels or upsetting people, by posting inflammatory or off topic messages in an online community, just for amusement.
cards.quote: an Internet troll is a person who deliberately sows discord on the Internet by starting quarrels or upsetting people, by posting inflammatory or off topic messages in an online community, just for amusement.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Since trolls thrive on attention, the best way to discourage trolls is ____ to their comments.
cards.back: Since trolls thrive on attention, the best way to discourage trolls is not to pay any attention to their comments.
cards.quote: Since trolls thrive on attention, the best way to discourage trolls is not to pay any attention to their comments.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For concerns related to data and bandwidth, ____ may be avoided.
cards.back: For concerns related to data and bandwidth, very large attachments may be avoided.
cards.quote: For concerns related to data and bandwidth, very large attachments may be avoided.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Give examples of synchronous and asynchronous communication.
cards.back: Whether the communication is synchronous (happening in real time like chat, audio/video calls) or asynchronous (like email, forum post or comments), we should be polite and non-aggressive in our communication.
cards.quote: Whether the communication is synchronous (happening in real time like chat, audio/video calls) or asynchronous (like email, forum post or comments), we should be polite and non-aggressive in our communication.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: On receiving junk email (called ____), neither reply nor open any attachment in such email.
cards.back: On receiving junk email (called Spam), neither reply nor open any attachment in such email.
cards.quote: On receiving junk email (called Spam), neither reply nor open any attachment in such email.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: We should be cautious while making a comment, replying or writing an email or forum post as such acts decide our ____ over a period of time.
cards.back: We should be cautious while making a comment, replying or writing an email or forum post as such acts decide our credibility over a period of time.
cards.quote: We should be cautious while making a comment, replying or writing an email or forum post as such acts decide our credibility over a period of time.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are social media?
cards.back: Social media are websites or applications that enable their users to participate in social networking by creating and sharing content with others in the community.
cards.quote: Social media are websites or applications that enable their users to participate in social networking by creating and sharing content with others in the community.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: The minimum one can do is to have ____ password.
cards.back: The minimum one can do is to have strong and frequently changed password.
cards.quote: The minimum one can do is to have strong and frequently changed password.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Never share personal credentials like ____ with others.
cards.back: Never share personal credentials like username and password with others.
cards.quote: Never share personal credentials like username and password with others.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Never arrange to ____ because it may not be safe.
cards.back: Never arrange to meet an online friend because it may not be safe.
cards.quote: Never arrange to meet an online friend because it may not be safe.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is sensitive data?
cards.back: Elements of data that can cause substantial harm, embarrassment, inconvenience and unfairness to an individual, if breached or compromised, is called sensitive data.
cards.quote: Elements of data that can cause substantial harm, embarrassment, inconvenience and unfairness to an individual, if breached or compromised, is called sensitive data.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Give examples of sensitive data.
cards.back:
biometric information
health information
financial information
other personal documents, images or audios or videos
cards.quote: Examples of sensitive data include biometric information, health information, financial information, or other personal documents, images or audios or videos.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is Intellectual Property?
cards.back: Intellectual Property refers to the inventions, literary and artistic expressions, designs and symbols, names and logos.
cards.quote: Intellectual Property refers to the inventions, literary and artistic expressions, designs and symbols, names and logos.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How is Intellectual Property legally protected?
cards.back:
copyrights
patents
trademarks
cards.quote: Intellectual Property is legally protected through copyrights, patents, trademarks,etc.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Executing IPR for a software: what protects its code, its functional expression, and its name and logo?
cards.back:
Code of the software will be protected by a copyright
Functional expression of the idea will be protected by a patent
The name and logo of the software will come under a registered trademark
cards.quote: Code of the software will be protected by a copyright Functional expression of the idea will be protected by a patent The name and logo of the software will come under a registered trademark

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is copyright?
cards.back: Copyright grants legal rights to creators for their original works like writing, photograph, audio recordings, video, sculptures, architectural works, computer software, and other creative works like literary and artistic work.
cards.quote: Copyright grants legal rights to creators for their original works like writing, photograph, audio recordings, video, sculptures, architectural works, computer software, and other creative works like literary and artistic work.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Copyrights are ____ granted to creators and authors.
cards.back: Copyrights are automatically granted to creators and authors.
cards.quote: Copyrights are automatically granted to creators and authors.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the rights a copyright holder alone can avail legally.
cards.back:
right to copy (reproduce) a work
right to create derivative works based upon it
right to distribute copies of the work to the public
right to publicly display or perform the work
cards.quote: The rights include right to copy (reproduce) a work, right to create derivative works based upon it, right to distribute copies of the work to the public, and right to publicly display or perform the work.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does copyright prevent others from doing?
cards.back: It prevents others from copying, using or selling the work.
cards.quote: It prevents others from copying, using or selling the work.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: To use other's copyrighted material, one needs to obtain a ____ from them.
cards.back: To use other's copyrighted material, one needs to obtain a license from them.
cards.quote: To use other's copyrighted material, one needs to obtain a license from them.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a patent give its owner?
cards.back: When a patent is granted, the owner gets an exclusive right to prevent others from using, selling, or distributing the protected invention.
cards.quote: When a patent is granted, the owner gets an exclusive right to prevent others from using, selling, or distributing the protected invention.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: For how many years does a patent protect an invention?
cards.back: A patent protects an invention for 20 years, after which it can be freely used.
cards.quote: A patent protects an invention for 20 years, after which it can be freely used.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a trademark?
cards.back: Trademark includes any visual symbol, word, name, design, slogan, label, etc., that distinguishes the brand or commercial enterprise, from other brands or commercial enterprises.
cards.quote: Trademark includes any visual symbol, word, name, design, slogan, label, etc., that distinguishes the brand or commercial enterprise, from other brands or commercial enterprises.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a license?
cards.back: A license is a type of contract or a permission agreement between the creator of an original work permitting someone to use their work, generally for some price
cards.quote: A license is a type of contract or a permission agreement between the creator of an original work permitting someone to use their work, generally for some price

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Licensing vs copyright: what is the difference?
cards.back: A license is a type of contract or a permission agreement between the creator of an original work permitting someone to use their work, generally for some price; whereas copyright is the legal rights of the creator for the protection of original work of different types.
cards.quote: A license is a type of contract or a permission agreement between the creator of an original work permitting someone to use their work, generally for some price; whereas copyright is the legal rights of the creator for the protection of original work of different types.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Only the ____ of a work can enter into a license agreement.
cards.back: Only the copyright owner of a work can enter into a license agreement.
cards.quote: Only the copyright owner of a work can enter into a license agreement.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a software license?
cards.back: A software license is an agreement that provides legally binding guidelines pertaining to the authorised use of digital material.
cards.quote: A software license is an agreement that provides legally binding guidelines pertaining to the authorised use of digital material.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does an End User License Agreement (EULA) contain?
cards.back: End User License Agreement (EULA) contains the dos and don'ts with respect to the software being purchased.
cards.quote: End User License Agreement (EULA) contains the dos and don'ts with respect to the software being purchased.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does a EULA cover?
cards.back: It covers all clauses of software purchase, viz., how many copies can be installed, whether source is available, whether it can be modified and redistributed and so on.
cards.quote: It covers all clauses of software purchase, viz., how many copies can be installed, whether source is available, whether it can be modified and redistributed and so on.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Failure to follow such guidelines is considered as an infringement of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), and is a ____.
cards.back: Failure to follow such guidelines is considered as an infringement of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), and is a criminal offence.
cards.quote: Failure to follow such guidelines is considered as an infringement of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), and is a criminal offence.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does plagiarism mean?
cards.back: Plagiarism means using other's work and not giving adequate citation for use.
cards.quote: Plagiarism means using other's work and not giving adequate citation for use.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Presenting someone else's idea or work as one's own idea or work is called ____.
cards.back: Presenting someone else's idea or work as one's own idea or work is called plagiarism.
cards.quote: Presenting someone else's idea or work as one's own idea or work is called plagiarism.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: If we copy some contents from Internet, but do not mention the source or the original creator, then it is considered as an act of ____.
cards.back: If we copy some contents from Internet, but do not mention the source or the original creator, then it is considered as an act of plagiarism.
cards.quote: If we copy some contents from Internet, but do not mention the source or the original creator, then it is considered as an act of plagiarism.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Even if we take contents that are open for public use, we should ____ to avoid plagiarism.
cards.back: Even if we take contents that are open for public use, we should cite the author or source to avoid plagiarism.
cards.quote: Even if we take contents that are open for public use, we should cite the author or source to avoid plagiarism.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is copyright infringement?
cards.back: Copyright infringement is when we use other person's work without obtaining their permission to use or we have not paid for it, if it is being sold.
cards.quote: Copyright infringement is when we use other person's work without obtaining their permission to use or we have not paid for it, if it is being sold.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Just because it is on the Internet, does not mean that it is ____.
cards.back: Just because it is on the Internet, does not mean that it is free for use.
cards.quote: Just because it is on the Internet, does not mean that it is free for use.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is trademark infringement?
cards.back: Trademark Infringement means unauthorised use of other's trademark on products and services.
cards.quote: Trademark Infringement means unauthorised use of other's trademark on products and services.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: When authors share their copyrighted works with others under ____, it allows others to use and even modify the content.
cards.back: When authors share their copyrighted works with others under public license, it allows others to use and even modify the content.
cards.quote: When authors share their copyrighted works with others under public license, it allows others to use and even modify the content.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Name the two popular categories of public licenses.
cards.back:
GNU General Public License (GPL)
Creative Commons (CC)
cards.quote: The GNU General Public License (GPL) and the Creative Commons (CC) are two popular categories of public licenses.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What kinds of work is Creative Commons (CC) used for?
cards.back: CC is used for all kind of creative works like websites, music, film, literature, etc.
cards.quote: CC is used for all kind of creative works like websites, music, film, literature, etc.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: CC enables the ____ of an otherwise copyrighted work.
cards.back: CC enables the free distribution of an otherwise copyrighted work.
cards.quote: CC enables the free distribution of an otherwise copyrighted work.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is GPL primarily designed for?
cards.back: GPL is primarily designed for providing public licence to a software.
cards.quote: GPL is primarily designed for providing public licence to a software.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is GNU GPL?
cards.back: GNU GPL is another free software license, which provides end users the freedom to run, study, share and modify the software, besides getting regular updates.
cards.quote: GNU GPL is another free software license, which provides end users the freedom to run, study, share and modify the software, besides getting regular updates.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What are CC licenses?
cards.back: CC licenses are a set of copyright licenses that give the recipients, rights to copy, modify and redistribute the creative material, but giving the authors, the liberty to decide the conditions of licensing.
cards.quote: CC licenses are a set of copyright licenses that give the recipients, rights to copy, modify and redistribute the creative material, but giving the authors, the liberty to decide the conditions of licensing.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is GPL, the most widely used free software license?
cards.back: GPL is the most widely used free software license which grants the recipients, rights to copy, modify and redistribute the software and that the same rights are preserved in all derivative works.
cards.quote: GPL is the most widely used free software license which grants the recipients, rights to copy, modify and redistribute the software and that the same rights are preserved in all derivative works.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: GPL vs freeware vs proprietary licenses: what distinguishes them?
cards.back: Users or companies who distribute GPL licensed works may charge a fee for copies or give them free of charge. This distinguishes the GPL license from freeware software licenses like Skype, Adobe Acrobat reader, etc. that allow copying for personal use but prohibit commercial distribution, or proprietary licenses where copying is prohibited by copyright law.
cards.quote: Users or companies who distribute GPL licensed works may charge a fee for copies or give them free of charge. This distinguishes the GPL license from freeware software licenses like Skype, Adobe Acrobat reader, etc. that allow copying for personal use but prohibit commercial distribution, or proprietary licenses where copying is prohibited by copyright law.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Many of the proprietary software that we use are sold commercially and their program code (source code) are ____.
cards.back: Many of the proprietary software that we use are sold commercially and their program code (source code) are not shared or distributed.
cards.quote: Many of the proprietary software that we use are sold commercially and their program code (source code) are not shared or distributed.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) allow users to do?
cards.back: Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) allow users to not only access but also to modify (or improve) them.
cards.quote: Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) allow users to not only access but also to modify (or improve) them.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is software piracy?
cards.back: Software piracy is the unauthorised use or distribution of software.
cards.quote: Software piracy is the unauthorised use or distribution of software.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: Software piracy amounts to which violation, whether for sale, free distribution or own use?
cards.back: It amounts to copyright infringement regardless of whether it is done for sale, for free distribution or for copier's own use.
cards.quote: It amounts to copyright infringement regardless of whether it is done for sale, for free distribution or for copier's own use.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: How does using pirated software affect the computer system and the country?
cards.back: Using a pirated software not only degrades the performance of a computer system, but also affects the software industry which in turn affects the economy of a country.
cards.quote: Using a pirated software not only degrades the performance of a computer system, but also affects the software industry which in turn affects the economy of a country.

source.section: Public Access and Open Source Software

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is Creative Commons?
cards.back: Creative Commons is a non-profit organisation (https://creativecommons.org/) that aims to build a publically accessible global platform where a range of creative and academic works are shared freely.
cards.quote: Creative Commons is a non-profit organisation (https://creativecommons.org/) that aims to build a publically accessible global platform where a range of creative and academic works are shared freely.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the Creative Commons organisation provide free of charge?
cards.back: The Creative Commons organisation provides Creative Commons (CC) licenses free of charge.
cards.quote: The Creative Commons organisation provides Creative Commons (CC) licenses free of charge.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What is a CC license?
cards.back: A CC license is a type of copyright license that enables the free distribution of anybody's copyrighted work.
cards.quote: A CC license is a type of copyright license that enables the free distribution of anybody's copyrighted work.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the CC BY (Attribution) license let others do?
cards.back: This license lets others distribute, remix, tweak, and build upon your work, even commercially, as long as they credit you for the original creation.
cards.quote: This license lets others distribute, remix, tweak, and build upon your work, even commercially, as long as they credit you for the original creation.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the CC BY-SA (Attribution-ShareAlike) license let others do?
cards.back: This license lets others remix, tweak, and build upon your work even for commercial purposes, as long as they credit you and license their new creations under the identical terms.
cards.quote: This license lets others remix, tweak, and build upon your work even for commercial purposes, as long as they credit you and license their new creations under the identical terms.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the CC BY-ND (Attribution-NoDerivs) license let others do?
cards.back: This license lets others reuse the work for any purpose, including commercially; however, it cannot be shared with others in adapted form, and credit must be provided to you.
cards.quote: This license lets others reuse the work for any purpose, including commercially; however, it cannot be shared with others in adapted form, and credit must be provided to you.

cards.subject: computer_science
cards.front: What does the CC BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial) license let others do?
cards.back: This license lets others remix, tweak, and build upon your work non-commercially, and although their new works must also acknowledge you and be non-commercial.
